trigger: an output handler's dtor re-enters ob_start(), pushing a new handler onto the same output stack while the old one is still being torn down
notes: handler = ecalloc(1, sizeof(php_output_handler)) at main/output.c:861 (arena); php_output_deactivate()'s teardown loop called php_output_handler_free(handler) (which efrees it) BEFORE zend_stack_del_top(&OG(handlers)), so a re-entrant ob_start() from the handler's own dtor that pushed a new stack entry made the subsequent del_top remove the NEW entry instead, leaving the already-freed handler's pointer still on the stack to be read on a later loop iteration

trigger: construct a Tidy/tidyNode object whose internal tidySetErrorBuffer() call fails
notes: intern is the object's zend_object, allocated through zend_object_alloc (Zend/zend_objects.c (master:190), arena - every PHP userland object); on a tidySetErrorBuffer() failure the constructor manually efree(intern)'d it in addition to raising an E_ERROR, but the engine's normal object-store teardown for a failed constructor also frees the same zend_object, a double free of the arena slot

trigger: printf()/vprintf() whose format-and-arguments rope collapses to a compile-time constant (e.g. no substitutions), so the compiler still emits a ZEND_COPY_TMP meant for a TMP_VAR
notes: op_array->literals is erealloc'd at Zend/zend_compile.c:598 (arena, request-lifetime compile buffer); zend_compile_func_printf() emitted a ZEND_COPY_TMP against rope_result even when it was IS_CONST (a literal-table entry, not a TMP_VAR slot), and ZEND_COPY_TMP's semantics assume ownership transfer of a TMP - applied to a shared literal, this let the runtime free/refcount-corrupt the persistent literal zval that later invocations of the same compiled function still reference

trigger: Windows: serve a file through the phar:// stream wrapper (php_stream/SAPI dispatch) down the highlight_file or execute-script code path
notes: on Windows the caller path-normalizes with fname = estrndup(fname, fname_len) at ext/phar/phar_object.c:618 (arena) and passes that same pointer into phar_file_action() as `arch`; the caller already efree()s it at its own cleanup label, but phar_file_action()'s highlight_file and execute-script branches ALSO called efree(arch) under #ifdef PHP_WIN32 - a double free of that estrndup'd arena string, now that an earlier refactor removed the early bailout that used to make those two frees mutually exclusive

trigger: parse a malformed URL through the PHP URI WHATWG parser
notes: lexbor's own allocator (lexbor_malloc/realloc/calloc/free, defaulting to plain malloc) is re-pointed at emalloc/erealloc/ecalloc/efree by php_lexbor_malloc() et al. (ext/lexbor/php_lexbor.c:31-47) via lexbor_memory_setup() at php_lexbor.c:61 - so lexbor's mraw-backed strings/URL buffers are zend-mm arena, not system malloc, even though lexbor is not in the ARENA-TEST.md bundled-library exception list. This commit imports an upstream lexbor fix for a UAF in the URL component/search-params buffer handling during malformed-URL processing

trigger: serialize() an SplHeap/SplPriorityQueue and then mutate the returned array's exposed property table
notes: the object's dynamic properties table is reached through zend_std_get_properties() on the zend_object (zend_object_alloc, Zend/zend_objects.c (master:190) - arena); __serialize() only Z_TRY_ADDREF'd that live table and exposed it directly to userland with its IS_INDIRECT elements intact, so later engine-internal mutation of the real property slots (or the object's destruction) could invalidate the exposed array out from under userland. Fixed by zend_array_dup()'ing (de-indirecting) a private copy instead

trigger: two processes race to compile and persist the same file into the opcache SHM; the losing process's freshly-compiled script (and its warnings) get discarded in favor of the winner's already-persisted copy
notes: EG(errors) is erealloc'd at Zend/zend.c:1489 (arena, per-request), and persistent_script->warnings = EG(errors) at ext/opcache/ZendAccelerator.c:1956/2181 makes the not-yet-persisted script alias that same array without copying it; free_persistent_script() on the losing process's discarded script efree'd each zend_error_info and the array itself, leaving EG(errors) a dangling pointer that zend_emit_recorded_errors() then read

trigger: gzopen() (ZEND_DEBUG builds) on a path where wrapper resolution ultimately leaves the returned stream NULL after orig_path was already set on a stream
notes: copy_of_path = pestrdup(path, persistent) at main/streams/streams.c:2299, then stream->orig_path = copy_of_path at line 2300 (arena for a non-persistent stream, see Zend/zend_alloc.h's pestrdup(s,0)); a ZEND_DEBUG-only fallback then pefree()'d copy_of_path directly whenever the function's `stream` ended up NULL, double-freeing the same pointer already owned (and freed on its own teardown path) by stream->orig_path

trigger: SCCP compile-time-evaluates a call to an internal function that both emits a warning/deprecation AND throws an exception
notes: result is the returned zval from the compile-time call; the zend_test repro's RETVAL_STRING("this is a non-interned string") at ext/zend_test/test.c (master:1536) builds it via zend_string_init (Zend/zend_string.h:188, arena) for a non-interned string. Two separate `if` blocks in ct_eval_func_call() (one for EG(exception), one for the SCCP warning-capture counter) each ran zval_ptr_dtor(result) when both conditions held simultaneously, releasing the same arena string twice

trigger: convert a phar to a different format (compress/convert) when the internal rename step (phar_rename_archive) errors out before reassigning the new filename
notes: a renamed phar's fname is spprintf(&newpath, 0, ...) (emalloc-backed, arena) at ext/phar/phar_object.c:2094, assigned via phar->fname = newpath at line 2098; when phar_rename_archive() errors out before reaching that assignment, phar->fname still just aliases source->fname (no fresh allocation), and the cleanup path's unconditional efree(phar->fname) freed the SAME string source (and later source itself) still owns

trigger: open a dba handle with a lock file (mixing an internal php_stream with the dba object) and let request shutdown destroy streams before the symbol table destroys the dba object
notes: the touched php_stream (info->fp/lock.fp) is non-persistent-arena via _php_stream_alloc (main/streams/streams.c (master:170)); its zend_resource is emalloc'd via ZVAL_NEW_RES at Zend/zend_types.h:1164 (same site as php-0044). Streams are destroyed in an early shutdown phase, but the dba zend_object (destroyed later, when the symbol table tears down) still called php_stream_close()/used info->fp afterward - a UAF on the already-freed stream/resource

trigger: a fatal error (bailout) occurs while the tracing JIT is compiling a trace
notes: the trace's SSA is zend_arena_calloc(&CG(arena), 1, sizeof(zend_tssa)) (ext/opcache/jit/zend_jit_trace.c:1431 and similar zend_arena_calloc calls for ssa) - the compiler/optimizer sub-arena, itself emalloc'd. A zend_bailout() mid-trace used to skip zend_arena_release(&CG(arena), checkpoint) and the op_array_ssa/jit_extension cleanup entirely, leaving SSA structures reachable from stale per-op_array JIT state for a later trace to read after the arena checkpoint memory is gone

trigger: parse a URI with soft errors while assigning the caller's $errors by-reference argument fails (e.g. the target is not a reference)
notes: errors is a zend_array built by the URI parser's error collector (array_init-style construction, arena via _zend_new_array/zend_hash_real_init, Zend/zend_hash.c:177/282); ZEND_TRY_ASSIGN_REF_ARR(errors_zv, ...) already consumes/frees the array when the by-reference assignment fails, but the old code unconditionally called zval_ptr_dtor(errors) afterward too, freeing the same arena array a second time

trigger: parse enough Uri\WhatWg\Url instances in one request to hit the periodic lexbor_mraw_clean() threshold while earlier parsed Url objects are still alive
notes: ext/uri hard-depends on ext/lexbor (PHP_ADD_EXTENSION_DEP(uri, lexbor), ext/uri/config.m4:43) and never calls its own lexbor_memory_setup(), so it inherits ext/lexbor's global redirection of lexbor_malloc/calloc to emalloc/ecalloc (ext/lexbor/php_lexbor.c:31-47,61) - the lexbor_mraw pool backing every parsed Uri\WhatWg\Url is zend-mm arena, not system malloc (8192B initial chunk per uri_parser_whatwg.c's lexbor_mraw_byte_size, exceeding the 3072B bin ceiling). The periodic lexbor_mraw_clean() call freed that whole arena chunk while earlier live Url objects still pointed into it

trigger: a nested try/finally where an inner finally's return also fails the outer function's declared return type, triggering DISCARD_EXCEPTION cleanup twice for the same incomplete RETURN
notes: return_value is EX_VAR(...) holding whatever refcounted value the incomplete RETURN produced - generically a zend_string (zend_string_alloc/init, Zend/zend_string.h:188), a zend_array (_zend_new_array, Zend/zend_hash.c (master:282)) or a zend_object (zend_object_alloc, Zend/zend_objects_API.h:92), all arena; ZEND_DISCARD_EXCEPTION's cleanup ran zval_ptr_dtor(return_value) without clearing the slot, so a subsequent zend_dispatch_try_catch_finally_helper pass that also cleans up the same incomplete RETURN dtor'd the same value again

trigger: a persistent pgsql connection is returned to the pool at request end while libpq's notice processor is still set to point at the freed per-request connection wrapper
notes: pgsql_link_handle *intern = zend_object_alloc(sizeof(pgsql_link_handle), class_type) at ext/pgsql/pgsql.c:160 (arena, PgSql\Connection object); PQsetNoticeProcessor(link, _php_pgsql_notice_handler, l) keeps a raw pointer to that per-request wrapper as libpq user-data on the underlying PGconn, which outlives the request when the connection is persistent, so a notice arriving before the next request re-sets the context called back into the already-freed wrapper

trigger: array_splice() on an array with a destructor-bearing element (or replacement values) that drops the array's own refcount to zero mid-operation
notes: in_hash's bucket store comes from zend_hash_real_init_*_ex()'s emalloc (Zend/zend_hash.c:177, arena); php_splice() rebuilt the array in place while running user destructors as elements were replaced/removed, and if that dropped the caller's own last reference to the array, zend_array_destroy() could free in_hash out from under the still-running splice. Fixed by a contributor/HT_ALLOW_COW_VIOLATION and checking GC_DELREF at the end

trigger: Generator::throw() on a generator that is already running (currently suspended inside a Fiber-based non-Generator delegate)
notes: the generator's delegate (a non-Generator Iterator) is a zend_object (zend_object_alloc, Zend/zend_objects.c (master:190) - arena); zend_generator_throw_exception() unconditionally released the delegate's values/execute state even while ZEND_GENERATOR_CURRENTLY_RUNNING, so if a Fiber suspended inside that delegate's own call stack, resuming the Fiber later dereferenced the already-released delegate object

trigger: resume a Generator a second time while it is still marked running because it delegates (yield from) to a non-Generator whose getIterator()/current() suspended and got resumed independently
notes: zend_generator is itself a zend_object (zend_object_alloc, Zend/zend_objects_API.h:92 - arena); ZEND_GENERATOR_CURRENTLY_RUNNING was only set after the delegated-value fast path, so a generator suspended inside a non-Generator delegate's own re-entrant resume wasn't marked running yet and could be resumed a second time concurrently, terminating execute_data the first resume was still using

trigger: a graceful Apache/mod_php restart tears down the JIT (zend_jit_shutdown) without clearing the module's global dasm_buf/dasm_ptr/dasm_end pointers, then a status query runs in a process that still shares that static state
notes: dasm_buf is set from the `buf` argument to zend_jit_startup(), which ext/opcache/ZendAccelerator.c:3270 passes as ZSMMG(reserved) - a region of opcache's own shared-memory segment (zend_shared_alloc, ext/opcache/zend_shared_alloc.c (master:383)), a separate blind arena from zend-mm. zend_jit_shutdown() released that SHM region without resetting the static dasm_buf/dasm_ptr/dasm_end/dasm_size globals, which zend_jit_status() then read as if still valid

trigger: SOAP-encode an object with typed attributes whose value also appears elsewhere in the structure as an href-able reference
notes: dummy is an xmlNode created by xmlNewNode/xmlAddChild inside the attribute loop and then immediately xmlUnlinkNode()'d and xmlFreeNode()'d in the same iteration (libxml2's own xmlMalloc, not zend-mm); the attribute's zval was still being registered into SOAP_GLOBAL(ref_map) as if it could be href-referenced later, so a later encoder pass that looked up the same zval in ref_map read the pointer to that already-freed dummy node

trigger: modify then flush a phar entry while an SplFileObject (or other open handle) still holds an open file pointer on that same entry
notes: the shared entry->fp is a non-persistent php_stream (_php_stream_alloc, main/streams/streams.c (master:170) - arena); phar_flush()/phar_tar_writeheaders_int() only preserved the stream from being freed when `!entry->is_modified && entry->fp_refcount`, so a MODIFIED entry with other open file pointers (fp_refcount > 0, e.g. an open SplFileObject) still had its shared stream freed while those other handles kept using it

trigger: convert/copy a phar archive whose entry content copy triggers the fp/cfp error-recovery hack
notes: entry->fp is a non-persistent php_stream (_php_stream_alloc, main/streams/streams.c (master:170) - arena, same object class as php-0089); phar_copy_file_contents() temporarily moved entry->fp into entry->cfp as an error-recovery hack that had no matching recovery code, so on the normal success path the same stream ended up reachable and freed through both entry->fp/cfp bookkeeping paths

trigger: an object that only uses the default zend_object_std_dtor free_obj handler, but is weakly referenced (WeakReference/WeakMap), is destroyed during request-shutdown symbol-table teardown
notes: the object is a zend_object (zend_object_alloc, Zend/zend_objects.c (master:190) - arena); the shutdown loop skipped calling free_obj entirely whenever it was exactly zend_object_std_dtor (an optimization, since std_dtor 'does nothing interesting'), but for an IS_OBJ_WEAKLY_REFERENCED object that skip also bypassed the weak-reference invalidation normally triggered on destruction, leaving WeakReference/WeakMap entries pointing at the object after its storage was freed

trigger: a userspace stream wrapper's write()/read() handler closes the same stream (fclose($this->stream) or similar) from inside the handler call
notes: stream is a non-persistent php_stream (_php_stream_alloc, main/streams/streams.c (master:170) - arena, same object class as php-0028/044/077); php_userstreamop_write/read called into the userland handler while the C stack still held `stream`, and a handler that closed the stream from inside itself freed that same struct out from under the caller, which kept dereferencing it afterward. Fixed with PHP_STREAM_FLAG_NO_FCLOSE around the callback

trigger: a static variable binds by reference to a value that is the same as (or storage-overlaps) the static variable slot itself
notes: variable_ptr holds an ordinary refcounted PHP value in the function's static-variables HashTable slot - generically a zend_string (Zend/zend_string.h:188) or zend_array (_zend_new_array, Zend/zend_hash.c (master:282)), both arena; i_zval_ptr_dtor(variable_ptr) ran before value was read/rewritten, so when variable_ptr and value aliased the same underlying allocation, destroying variable_ptr first freed the memory `value` was about to be read from

trigger: call PDO::setAttribute(PDO_FB_ATTR_DATE_FORMAT/...) on a PERSISTENT pdo_firebird connection, then let the request end and a later request reuse that persistent connection
notes: H->date_format was built with spprintf(&H->date_format, 0, "%s", ...) at ext/pdo_firebird/firebird_driver.c:886, always emalloc-backed (arena) regardless of persistence; H itself is pemalloc'd persistent (system-malloc) for a persistent PDO connection and survives across requests, so the arena string it pointed to became dangling the moment the request that set it ended and its arena chunk was reclaimed - exactly the arena-vs-persistent-container trap, inverted. Fixed by pestrndup(...,dbh->is_persistent)/pefree so a persistent handle's strings are persistent too

trigger: extract($array, EXTR_REFS) where an existing local variable being overwritten aliases the same reference as the array element replacing it
notes: orig_var is a symbol-table zval holding a generic refcounted value (zend_string, Zend/zend_string.h:188, or a zend_reference, Zend/zend_vm_def.h:9062, both arena); zval_ptr_dtor(orig_var) ran before ZVAL_REF(orig_var, Z_REF_P(entry)) read from entry, so when orig_var and entry ultimately referenced the same reference/value, destroying orig_var first freed the memory entry was about to be copied from. Fixed by a contributor

trigger: isset()/empty() on an ArrayObject/ArrayIterator offset whose offsetGet() returns a refcount-1 value
notes: value is the temporary zval returned by spl_array_read_dimension_ex() (ext/spl/spl_array.c) - a fresh refcounted value (e.g. zend_string via Zend/zend_string.h:188, arena) with refcount 1; the pre-fix code ran zval_ptr_dtor(&rv) - freeing that RC1 value - BEFORE evaluating zend_is_true(value)/Z_TYPE_P(value), reading the just-freed arena slot for the truthiness/null check

trigger: dl() a loadable module that registers a parent and child internal class, then unload/shut it down
notes: internal (ZEND_INTERNAL_CLASS) class entries are explicitly the NOT-arena case in the rulebook (persistent/internal class entries use __zend_malloc, Zend/zend_alloc.h (master:188) family, not zend-mm); clean_module_classes() destroyed a dl()'ed module's classes in hash (registration) order, so a parent class could be destroyed before its child even though the child's zend_class_entry still references structures (e.g. inherited property tables) owned by the parent

trigger: toggle the zend_test.observe_opline_in_zend_mm INI setting off during GSHUTDOWN/module teardown after it was previously enabled
notes: ZT_G(zend_test_heap) = malloc(4096) at ext/zend_test/test.c:680 - plain system malloc, since this buffer replaces the Zend MM heap it can't itself live inside that heap; the free+reset logic only ran from the INI on-modify handler, not from PHP_GSHUTDOWN_FUNCTION, so a heap left active past request/module shutdown (e.g. under magic_quotes_gpc=1's extra RINIT/RSHUTDOWN ordering) was read/freed inconsistently. Fixed by factoring the reset into zend_test_reset_heap() and calling it from GSHUTDOWN too

trigger: invoke a Closure (e.g. $closure()) whose underlying function carries attributes (e.g. #[\Deprecated]), creating a temporary __invoke trampoline that is later destroyed
notes: closure->func.common.attributes is pemalloc(sizeof(HashTable), persistent)'d in zend_add_attribute() at Zend/zend_attributes.c:418 (arena for a non-persistent function); zend_get_closure_invoke_method()'s `invoke->common = closure->func.common;` (Zend/zend_closures.c:467) aliases that same attributes table into the temporary invoke trampoline without incrementing its refcount, while the (then-existing) zend_free_trampoline macro in Zend/zend_object_handlers.h unconditionally GC_DELREF'd and zend_array_destroy()'d attributes on trampoline teardown - an unbalanced decrement that freed the closure's still-live, shared attributes table. Fixed by a contributor (and the matching now-unneeded GC_TRY_ADDREF in the separate __call-trampoline path), since attributes are compiler-owned for the function's whole lifetime

trigger: delete/unlink a phar entry (or otherwise let it be removed from the manifest) while a PharFileInfo object still references it
notes: the phar_entry_info is stored via zend_hash_add_mem(&mydata->manifest, ...) at ext/phar/phar.c:1243 (arena, same object class as php-0061); PharFileInfo::__construct just cached entry_info->entry without any refcounting, so removing the entry from the manifest (e.g. unlink()) could free that slot while the PharFileInfo object still pointed at it. Fixed by a contributor>fp_refcount to keep it pinned in the manifest for the object's lifetime

trigger: a fetch-class constructor (or object __destruct/__toString reached during fetching) mutates PDOStatement's default-fetch ctor_args or class while a fetchAll() call is using it
notes: stmt->fetch.cls.ctor_args is a zend_array (bucket store via zend_hash_real_init_*_ex()'s emalloc, Zend/zend_hash.c:177 - arena); fetchAll() cached old_ctor_args by raw ZVAL_COPY_VALUE (no refcount) while running user code (the constructor) that could replace/free stmt->fetch.cls.ctor_args, leaving old_ctor_args a dangling reference to an array that had already been destroyed

trigger: let both the PDO driver (database) object and a PDOStatement become unreachable together, so the garbage collector - not refcounting - decides destruction order and frees the driver object first
notes: S->H is the pdo_firebird_db_handle assigned at ext/pdo_firebird/firebird_driver.c:1051 (`H = dbh->driver_data = pecalloc(1,sizeof(*H),dbh->is_persistent)`) - arena for a normal, non-persistent connection; firebird_stmt_dtor() dereferenced S->H unconditionally, but a GC-driven (non-refcount, cycle collector) destruction order can free the driver object - and its H - before the statement object, leaving S->H dangling

trigger: assign by reference to a typed property/variable whose OLD value's destructor re-enters and reassigns the same reference
notes: ref is a zend_reference, emalloc'd at Zend/zend_vm_def.h:9062 (`ref = (zend_reference*)emalloc(sizeof(zend_reference))`, arena); the old code did zval_ptr_dtor(&ref->val) (which can invoke a __destruct running arbitrary code that reassigns ref->val itself) and only afterward wrote ZVAL_COPY_VALUE(&ref->val, val), so a reentrant reassignment during the destructor was clobbered/read stale. zend_safe_assign_to_variable_noref()/zval_ptr_safe_dtor() now null the slot before the destructor can run

trigger: importNode() a source attribute node whose namespace must be resolved/attached against the DESTINATION document's root element
notes: xmlSearchNsByHref(nodep->doc, root, ...) searched the SOURCE document's namespace list against `root`, which actually belongs to `docp` (the destination document); the resulting/created xmlNs (libxml2's own xmlMalloc, not zend-mm) then got parked via php_libxml_set_old_ns(nodep->doc, nsptr) on the wrong document's oldNs list, so it could be freed with a document other than the one whose live tree still points at it

trigger: initialize-as-array a zval whose previous refcounted value's destructor re-enters and touches the same zval slot
notes: zv holds an ordinary refcounted PHP value - generically a zend_string (Zend/zend_string.h:188) or zend_object (zend_object_alloc, Zend/zend_objects_API.h:92), both arena; the old code ran zval_ptr_dtor(zv) directly - which can invoke a __destruct that reads/reassigns the same zv - before overwriting it with ZVAL_ARR(zv, arr). Fixed by a contributor `garbage`, nulling zv first, and only then destroying garbage

trigger: convert/rename a phar to a name that collides with an already-open, empty (zero-entry) phar archive of the same final name
notes: mydata (a phar_archive_data) is ecalloc(1, sizeof(phar_archive_data)) at ext/phar/phar.c:1440 for a non-cached phar (arena); phar_rename_archive() reused an existing pphar object (`phar = pphar;`) in place of the freshly-parsed one without incrementing pphar->refcount, so a later release of one of the now-multiple owners dropped the refcount to zero and freed the still-referenced, reused phar_archive_data - a prior (edae2431) attempt at fixing this leak/double-free had gotten the refcount direction wrong

trigger: an iconv stream filter whose second processing stage (the flush/finalize step, flags != PSFS_FLAG_NORMAL) fails after the first stage's bucket loop already ran
notes: bucket = (php_stream_bucket*)pemalloc(sizeof(php_stream_bucket), is_persistent) at main/streams/filter.c:76 (arena for a non-persistent stream); the shared `out_failure:` label always ran php_stream_bucket_delref(bucket) on whichever bucket the first while-loop last set, but the second stage's failure path shares that same label despite `bucket` no longer being relevant/owned there - a stale pointer from an already fully-processed (already delref'd) first-loop iteration got delref'd again

trigger: register a user filter whose name already has a registered factory, so the second registration step fails
notes: fdat = ecalloc(1, sizeof(struct php_user_filter_data)) at ext/standard/user_filters.c:516; on the second failure the entry stayed in BG(user_filter_map) whose dtor had already freed it

trigger: function JIT compiling a deref of a register-allocated typed operand
notes: the JIT-emitted store targets an EX_VAR slot in the current execute_data, which lives in a VM stack page emalloc'd by zend_vm_stack_new_page (Zend/zend_execute.c (master:194)), or in the zend_reference (emalloc) it dereferences

trigger: reload the document (DOMDocument::load) while a DOMNamedNodeMap iterator is live
notes: the freed object is doc->dict, a libxml2 xmlDict allocated by libxml2's own xmlMalloc (php-src never calls xmlMemSetup); the objmap wrapper next to it IS arena (efree(objmap) at ext/dom/php_dom.c:1135) but is not what dangles

trigger: call __construct() again on a DOM node that is already inserted in a document
notes: the node's name/content strings still point into the old document's xmlDict, and the fix adds xmlSetTreeDoc(); libxml2 tree memory comes from xmlMalloc, not emalloc libxml2 keeps its own allocator here: php-src never calls xmlMemSetup, which appears only in the Windows export list ext/libxml/php_libxml2.def (master:441).

trigger: readline_info('line_buffer', $long) after readline_write_history(), so rl_extend_line_buffer reallocates
notes: oldstr aliased rl_line_buffer, which libreadline allocates and reallocates with its own xmalloc/xrealloc; the fix's own workaround uses strdup()/free() rather than estrdup()/efree() (ext/readline/readline.c:183-198), which is the tell

trigger: a heredoc inside a script compiled with zend.multibyte encoding translation, nesting zend_save_lexical_state()
notes: SCNG(script_filtered) is the emalloc'd encoding-translated copy of the whole script - the pre-fix code frees it with efree() at Zend/zend_language_scanner.l:278, and it is then restored from the saved state (line 284) and used again

trigger: unset($arrayObject[$k]) where the removed value's destructor mutates the same ArrayObject
notes: the destructor runs before the bucket is marked UNDEF, so it can free/rehash the HashTable's bucket array, which is emalloc'd at Zend/zend_hash.c (master:224) (HT_SET_DATA_ADDR(ht, emalloc(HT_SIZE_EX(...))))

trigger: session_encode() where serializing one value runs userland code that mutates $_SESSION
notes: PS_ENCODE_LOOP (ext/session/php_session.h:294) iterates the session HashTable unprotected; its bucket array is emalloc'd at Zend/zend_hash.c (master:224) and is reallocated out from under the iterator

trigger: serialize() a SplDoublyLinkedList whose element values have __sleep/__serialize that mutate the list
notes: elements are spl_ptr_llist_element *elem = emalloc(sizeof(spl_ptr_llist_element)) at ext/spl/spl_dllist.c:162,182; php_var_serialize can free current->next before the loop reads it

trigger: cloneNode()/insertBefore() where a validity check fails after the document reference was already switched
notes: the early document-ref switch can drop the last ref on the old xmlDoc, which php_libxml_decrement_doc_ref destroys with xmlFreeDoc (libxml2 xmlMalloc memory); the php_libxml_ref_obj wrapper beside it is arena but is not the dangling object libxml2 keeps its own allocator here: php-src never calls xmlMemSetup, which appears only in the Windows export list ext/libxml/php_libxml2.def (master:441).

trigger: serialize() a SplObjectStorage whose stored objects' __sleep mutates the storage
notes: element->inf is a zval inside the intern->storage HashTable, whose bucket array is emalloc'd at Zend/zend_hash.c (master:224); php_var_serialize can rehash it, so the pointer read afterwards is stale

trigger: appendChild()/insertBefore() passing a DOMDocument as the child node

notes: get_zval_xmlrpc_type fills `val` via ZVAL_COPY_VALUE (ext/xmlrpc/xmlrpc-epi-php.c:1371/1374, no addref - bare alias of the caller's zend_string/zend_object); PHP_to_XMLRPC_worker calls get_zval_xmlrpc_type(in_val,&val) at :509 then (pre-fix) convert_to_long(&val) at :538, which zend_string_release()s the aliased value in place, leaving the original in_val referencing already-freed arena memory

trigger: pg_connect()/pg_pconnect() with a non-string argument (e.g. an object with __toString) for host/port/options/tty/dbname
notes: args = safe_emalloc(ZEND_NUM_ARGS(), sizeof(zval), 0) at ext/pgsql/pgsql.c:1283 is filled by _zend_get_parameters_array_ex via ZVAL_COPY_VALUE (Zend/zend_API.c:120) - a bare alias of the live VM argument-stack zvals, no addref; convert_to_string_ex(&args[i]) at pgsql.c:1303 (pre-fix) can zval_dtor a non-string arg in place, freeing the caller's still-referenced value through this unowned alias - the fix replaces it with the non-destructive ZVAL_STR(&args[i], zval_get_string(&args[i]))

trigger: dba_open()/dba_popen() with a non-string argument (e.g. an object with __toString) among the handler args
notes: same anti-pattern as php-0294 (pgsql, same wave of fixes): args = safe_emalloc(ac, sizeof(zval), 0) at ext/dba/dba.c:653 is filled via ZVAL_COPY_VALUE (Zend/zend_API.c, bare alias of the VM argument stack, no addref); convert_to_string_ex(&args[i]) at dba.c:662 (pre-fix) can zval_dtor a non-string arg in place through that unowned alias, freeing the caller's still-referenced value - replaced with the non-destructive ZVAL_STR(&args[i], zval_get_string(&args[i]))

trigger: error_reporting() is called with an object argument whose __toString() recursively calls error_reporting() again
notes: pre-fix, Zend/zend_builtin_functions.c:730 released p->value (zend_string_release, a zval_get_string-built arena string) then, still on the RHS of the same statement at :733, called zval_get_string(err) again to build the new value - if err is an object, this __toString() call can re-enter error_reporting() and observe/re-release the already-freed p->value before the outer call's assignment completes; the fix computes new_val = zval_get_string(err) BEFORE touching p->value at all

trigger: phpdbg compiles the same file handle twice (its caller re-invokes cleanup/compile on a zend_file_handle already torn down here)
notes: zend_file_handle_dtor (Zend/zend_stream.c:302) already null-guards fh->opened_path/fh->filename after release, but its switch(fh->type) close path (e.g. ZEND_HANDLE_STREAM: fh->handle.stream.closer(fh->handle.stream.handle)) has no such guard - a stream handle is typically a non-persistent php_stream (main/streams/streams.c:170, persistent_id NULL -> zend-mm-bin); a second zend_file_handle_dtor(file) call with fh->type unchanged re-closes it. The fix sets file->type = -1 after the dtor here so a later dtor call matches no switch case

trigger: declare a class/global constant whose value expression is a not-yet-evaluated AST (e.g. involves another constant), compiled/executed more than once (opcache, or the same op_array run twice)
notes: c.value is filled via ZVAL_COPY_VALUE(&c.value, val) at Zend/zend_vm_def.h:7173 (pre-fix) - a bare alias (no addref) of the op_array's own persistent literal slot val, whose IS_CONSTANT_AST content is a zend_ast created via zend_arena_alloc(&CG(arena)/CG(ast_arena),...) (compiler sub-arena, see Zend/zend_ast.c:32); zval_update_constant_ex(&c.value,...) evaluates/frees the shared AST in place, leaving the op_array's own literal (reused on every future call of the same function/every request under opcache) pointing at freed arena memory. Fixed by ZVAL_COPY (proper addref via the AST's own ast_ref refcount) instead

trigger: call a generator method (bound $this) in a way where the caller's own call frame does not itself own a RELEASE_THIS reference
notes: This is a zend_object (every PHP object is arena, zend_objects_new/zend_object_alloc); pre-fix, Zend/zend_generators.c checked ZEND_CALL_INFO(call) & ZEND_CALL_RELEASE_THIS (the CALLER frame's flag, about to be torn down) to decide whether to addref call->This for the generator's own long-lived saved execute_data, so the generator could end up with no addref of its own while the caller frame released its reference at teardown - leaving the generator's saved $this dangling on resume. Fixed by a contributor

trigger: SplDoublyLinkedList::offsetSet() with an out-of-range index
notes: value is the caller's zval, parsed via zend_parse_parameters ("z") as a borrowed/not-owned reference; ext/spl/spl_dllist.c:833 (pre-fix) called zval_ptr_dtor(value) on this out-of-range path, an extra unowned decref - the VM stack still holds and will independently decref the same refcounted value (any PHP zval type, all zend_object_alloc/zend_string_init family - arena) when the call frame tears down, freeing it a second time

trigger: imagecreatefromwebp() on a file whose WebPGetInfo() call fails
notes: gdMalloc/gdRealloc/gdFree are #define'd to emalloc/erealloc/efree at ext/gd/libgd/gdhelpers.h:16-19; filedata is built via gdRealloc in the read loop (ext/gd/libgd/gd_webp.c:49), and at the end of the function (pre-fix) gdFree(filedata) at :94 is immediately followed by gdFree(temp) at :97 - temp aliases the same pointer as filedata after the loop exits, so this frees the (input-sized, routinely >3KB) buffer twice

trigger: wddx_deserialize() a malformed <boolean> value, followed by further XML events for the same stack entry
notes: ent is a st_entry (emalloc'd, confirmed by the paired efree(ent) calls at ext/wddx/wddx.c:1038 and :1097); the ST_BOOLEAN malformed-value branch efree'd ent directly at :1097 while only decrementing stack->top, leaving later SAX callbacks (which re-derive the current entry via wddx_stack_top) able to revisit/re-free the same slot - compounded by a real type-confusion bug in the same function, `switch (Z_TYPE_P(ent))` at :1054 applying the zval Z_TYPE_P macro to a st_entry* (not a zval), fixed to `switch (ent->type)`. The commit also adds the same varname-double-free guard as php-0289's ST_BOOLEAN handler in the neighboring EL_VAR case

trigger: Generator::send() a value after the generator delegated to an inner generator/iterator via yield from
notes: generator->send_target / root->send_target is a raw zval* pointing into a generator's own VM stack page (zend_vm_stack_new_page -> emalloc(size) at Zend/zend_execute.c:151, ZEND_VM_GENERATOR_STACK_PAGE_SLOTS=256 * sizeof(zval) = 4096B, over the 3KB small-bin cutoff); pre-fix, Generator::send() and zend_generator_cleanup_unfinished_execution both did Z_TRY_DELREF_P(...->send_target) on this pointer even though yield from delegation can leave it referencing a VM stack page that was already freed/reused by the inner generator's own teardown - the fix drops these premature dereferences entirely

trigger: a request using opcache with fast_shutdown enabled ends normally
notes: ZCG(cwd) = estrndup(cwd, ZCG(cwd_len)) (ext/opcache/ZendAccelerator.c, e.g. line 165/186 pre-fix) - a request-lifetime emalloc'd string; accel_deactivate() (pre-fix) freed it at the very end of the function, AFTER zend_accel_fast_shutdown() (which sets CG(unclean_shutdown)=1 and does a bulk/non-graceful teardown of request-scoped tables); the fix moves the efree(ZCG(cwd))/NULL reset to the top of accel_deactivate, before fast_shutdown's bulk teardown runs

trigger: unserialize() a crafted SplObjectStorage payload with multiple entries, where a later entry's parse fails/branches after an earlier entry's local zvals were released
notes: entry/inf are per-iteration local zvals holding arbitrary unserialized PHP values (any zend_object_alloc/zend_string_init family - arena); ext/spl/spl_observer.c:823-824 (pre-fix) called zval_ptr_dtor(&entry)/zval_ptr_dtor(&inf) after their content was copied into the new SplObjectStorage element, without resetting them to UNDEF - since the loop reuses these locals, a later parse failure or cleanup path touching the stale (already-released) entry/inf reads or re-releases freed memory

trigger: unserialize() a crafted ArrayObject/ArrayIterator payload whose inner array parse can reentrantly observe the object's own array property
notes: intern->array is a zval property on the spl_array_object (a zend_object, arena); ext/spl/spl_array.c:1780 (pre-fix) called zval_ptr_dtor(&intern->array) then, without resetting it to UNDEF, immediately called php_var_unserialize(&intern->array,...) to refill it - any reentrant read of intern->array during that parse (e.g. a crafted backreference) observes the dangling freed value; fix adds ZVAL_UNDEF(&intern->array) between the two calls

trigger: wddx_deserialize() a crafted <array> element containing a field named php_class_name
notes: ext/wddx/wddx.c:980 (pre-fix) triggered the php_class_name special-case handling whenever ent1->varname matched, without checking ent2->type == ST_STRUCT first; that branch zval_ptr_dtor(&ent2->data) (freeing the current array's HashTable, _zend_new_array family) at :1006 and reassigns ent2->data = obj (a freshly object_init_ex'd instance) at :1009 - for an ST_ARRAY entry this silently swaps an array for an object in place while ent2->type stays ST_ARRAY, so later processing keyed on ent2->type keeps treating ent2->data as an array (Z_ARRVAL_P) when it is now an object

trigger: Collator::sortWithSortKeys() on a by-ref array argument
notes: sortKeyIndxBuf[j].zstr entries are built earlier in the function from the ORIGINAL array's own zvals (any zend_string/refcounted value, arena); ext/intl/collator/collator_sort.c (pre-fix) called zval_ptr_dtor(array) - freeing that original array's HashTable and its element zvals - THEN array_init(array) and only afterward looped reading sortKeyIndxBuf[j].zstr (dangling into the just-freed array) to build the sorted result. Fixed by ZVAL_COPY_VALUE'ing the original into a local `garbage` zval, building the new array first, and only then zval_ptr_dtor'ing garbage

trigger: sprintf()/vsprintf() with a width or precision specifier greater than INT_MAX, using the array-arguments (vsprintf) form
notes: newargs = safe_emalloc(argc, sizeof(zval), 0) at ext/standard/formatted_print.c:427; two error paths (width-too-large and precision-too-large) each had the SAME `if (newargs) efree(newargs);` guard duplicated back to back in the pre-fix source (e.g. lines 518/522 and 540/544), freeing the same emalloc'd argv-copy array twice

trigger: a persistent stream with an attached context is torn down at a subsequent request's stream-persistence cleanup
notes: stream->ctx is a zend_resource*, emalloc'd (ZVAL_NEW_RES -> emalloc(sizeof(zend_resource)), Zend/zend_types.h) and freed via zend_list_delete; main/streams/streams.c:85-86 (pre-fix, forget_persistent_resource_id_numbers) called zend_list_delete(stream->ctx) without resetting stream->ctx to NULL, so any later `if (stream->ctx)` check on this persistent stream (which itself outlives the request) treats the freed resource pointer as still valid

trigger: the opcache Windows shared-memory segment is detached (module shutdown or reinit)
notes: mapping_base is the process's view of opcache's shared-memory segment (Windows MapViewOfFile, a distinct blind arena from zend-mm, matching the opcache-shm category); ext/opcache/shared_alloc_win32.c's detach_segment (pre-fix) called UnmapViewOfFile(mapping_base)/CloseHandle(memfile)/CloseHandle(memory_mutex) without clearing the corresponding static globals, so a later attach/detach cycle in the same process could read stale handles/pointer into the already-unmapped segment

trigger: the CGI/FastCGI or LiteSPEED request loop processes more than one request in the same worker process
notes: SG(request_info).path_translated is estrdup'd per request (sapi/cgi/cgi_main.c:1398/2254); in the persistent worker loop (cgi/fastcgi/litespeed all reuse one process across requests), efree(SG(request_info).path_translated) at multiple sites (e.g. cgi_main.c:2356, :2490; lsapi_main.c) was not followed by resetting the field to NULL, so the next request in the same process could see and re-free (or read) the same stale pointer

trigger: heap teardown at request/process shutdown while huge (>2MB) allocations are still outstanding
notes: each zend_mm_huge_list bookkeeping node is itself allocated via zend_mm_alloc_heap(heap, sizeof(zend_mm_huge_list),...) at Zend/zend_alloc.c:1635 (small, zend-mm-bin); zend_mm_shutdown (pre-fix) walked heap->huge_list freeing each node's huge block via zend_mm_chunk_free without clearing heap->huge_list until the loop finished, so any reentrant walk of heap->huge_list during that loop (e.g. debug/leak-tracking code, mirroring zend_mm_check_leaks's own use of the same field just above) would see partially-freed list nodes

trigger: unserialize() a crafted SplDoublyLinkedList payload containing a backreference into an element that was pushed onto the list
notes: elem is an ALLOC_INIT_ZVAL'd local (arena, any PHP value); ext/spl/spl_dllist.c (pre-fix) pushed it onto intern->llist via spl_ptr_llist_push without ever calling var_push_dtor(&var_hash, &elem) to register it with the unserializer's own backreference-cleanup list, so a later r/R backreference in the same payload or var_hash's own teardown could free/reference it inconsistently with the list's copy - same class as php-0280/0306/0307/0317

trigger: unserialize() a crafted SplObjectStorage payload containing a backreference into an attached object or its info value
notes: pentry/pinf are ALLOC_INIT_ZVAL'd locals (arena, any PHP value) populated by php_var_unserialize; ext/spl/spl_observer.c (pre-fix) never called var_push_dtor(&var_hash, &pentry)/&pinf after a successful parse, before using them to look up/attach the SplObjectStorage entry - a later backreference to the same offset in the same payload, or var_hash's own cleanup, could act on them inconsistently. Companion to php-0306 (bug #71313, a related but later SplObjectStorage unserialize UAF in the same function)

trigger: unserialize() a top-level payload starting with an R: (reference) or r: backreference token
notes: php_var_unserialize(&return_value,...) can internally repoint the local return_value pointer at a different zval (var_hash's own backreference-table entry) for a top-level r/R token, leaving the engine's actual output slot (old_rval) never updated; ext/standard/var.c's PHP_FUNCTION(unserialize) (pre-fix) had no handling for return_value != old_rval, so old_rval kept stale/uninitialized content while the swapped-in value (any PHP zval, arena) was left to var_hash's teardown (PHP_VAR_UNSERIALIZE_DESTROY) - a UAF once the caller reads the real return value. Distinct from php-0280 (bug #70436, the failure-path var_push_dtor gap in the same function)

trigger: a fatal/signal handler reads PG(last_error_message)/PG(last_error_file) while a concurrent error report is freeing and replacing them
notes: PG(last_error_message)/PG(last_error_file) are strdup'd (main/main.c:1003 pre-fix, and file similarly) and free()'d with plain libc free() (:989, :993 pre-fix) - proof they are outside zend-mm; pre-fix, the global still held the pointer for the full duration of free(), so a signal handler interrupting mid-free (or between free and reassignment) would read a use-after-freed pointer. Fixed by a contributor, nulling the global FIRST, then freeing the local - making the window signal-safe without needing HANDLE_BLOCK_INTERRUPTIONS

trigger: JIT-compiled code accesses a deprecated constant whose deprecation handler throws/raises an exception
notes: EX_VAR(opline->result.var) resolves into the current call's VM stack frame (ZEND_CALL_VAR, Zend/zend_compile.h:756), itself an emalloc'd zend_vm_stack page (Zend/zend_execute.c, 16K-slot main stack, well over 3KB); ext/opcache/jit/zend_jit_vm_helpers.c (pre-fix) returned NULL on EG(exception) without writing that result slot, leaving it holding whatever was there before - the VM's normal zval_ptr_dtor_nogc cleanup on the opcode's result then treats that leftover/garbage content as a live zval and can free an arbitrary address

trigger: JIT-compiled register-based FETCH_OBJ_R throws while reading a property (read_property returns &EG(uninitialized_zval))
notes: same class as php-0323 (uninitialized VM/JIT result slot later dtor'd as garbage), different path: when the JIT keeps the FETCH_OBJ_R result in a CPU register (Z_MODE(res_addr)==IS_REG) rather than the VM stack slot directly, the plain zend_jit_check_exception(jit) helper (pre-fix) didn't initialize the eventual result slot on the exception path; fixed by calling zend_jit_check_exception_undef_result(jit, opline) instead, which does. Result slot is the same emalloc'd zend_vm_stack page family as php-0323

trigger: JIT-compiled code where a temporary variable, live only in a register (never stored to its VM slot), spans an opcode range that can throw and is covered by the op_array's live_range table
notes: the temp var's VM slot lives in the current call's zend_vm_stack page (emalloc'd, Zend/zend_execute.c, main stack 16K slots - zend-mm-large); pre-fix, ext/opcache/jit/zend_jit.c's register allocator (zend_jit_allocate_registers) could decide such a temp needs no ZREG_STORE (kept only in a CPU register) even when an exception thrown mid-range would make the VM's live_range-driven cleanup run zval_ptr_dtor on that VM slot - reading and freeing whatever stale/leftover content was already sitting there instead of the actual value (own comment: "Check if a temporary variable may be freed by exception handler")

trigger: JIT-compiled ZEND_BOOL/JMPZNZ or FETCH_DIM_R on a possibly-undefined operand raises the undefined-variable warning/exception
notes: same class as php-0323/php-0324 (uninitialized VM-stack result slot later dtor'd as garbage on an exception path), a third distinct call site: zend_jit_type_check_undef's exception check (pre-fix, always zend_jit_check_exception) didn't initialize the opcode's result slot for callers whose result can be left undefined; fixed by a contributor (which ZVAL_UNDEFs the EX_VAR result slot) for zend_jit_bool_jmpznz and zend_jit_fetch_dim_read specifically. Result slot is the same emalloc'd zend_vm_stack page family

trigger: new DateTime($str) or DateTime::modify() where the parse produced no warnings or errors
notes: err is a timelib_error_container allocated by timelib (ext/date/lib/timelib.h (master:305)-309 defines timelib_malloc = malloc); update_errors_warnings called timelib_error_container_dtor on it and the caller then read err->error_count

trigger: timezone_open()/new DateTime with a 5-character offset that is not HH:MM, e.g. '+1234'
notes: the scanner reads begin[2] and begin+3 past the token; the scan buffer is in.str = timelib_malloc((e - s) + YYMAXFILL) at ext/date/lib/parse_date.re:1858, i.e. libc malloc via timelib_malloc (ext/date/lib/timelib.h (master:305))

trigger: strtotime()/DateTime with a crafted meridian token (bug #75055)
notes: same timelib scan buffer, in.str = timelib_malloc((e - s) + YYMAXFILL) at ext/date/lib/parse_date.re:1858; the meridian scanner ran past the token end

trigger: unserialize() of a crafted DateTimeZone with a mismatched timezone_type
notes: the serialized members are zvals in an emalloc'd HashTable (Zend/zend_hash.c (master:224)); a timezone_type of one kind was used to interpret a timezone value of another, reinterpreting a zval payload

trigger: unserialize() of a crafted DateTime whose 'date' member is converted while 'timezone' is re-read
notes: convert_to_string(*z_date) can rehash/reallocate the unserialized HashTable's bucket array (emalloc, Zend/zend_hash.c (master:224)), invalidating the z_timezone pointer fetched from it

trigger: strtotime() with a truncated meridian token (bug #67253)
notes: same timelib scan buffer from timelib_malloc at ext/date/lib/parse_date.re:1858 (timelib_malloc = malloc, ext/date/lib/timelib.h (master:305))

trigger: convert a UnicodeString longer than INT32_MAX/3 UTF-16 units to a PHP string
notes: capacity = from.length() * 3 overflows int32_t, then u8res = zend_string_alloc(capacity, 0) (ext/intl/intl_convertcpp.cpp:69) is undersized and u_strToUTF8WithSub writes past it

trigger: NumberFormatter::format(INF) or any conversion that fills the buffer exactly
notes: u_strToUTF8WithSub was given capacity rather than capacity + 1 for the buffer from zend_string_alloc(capacity, 0) (ext/intl/intl_convertcpp.cpp:72), so on the exact-fit path ICU reported overflow and left the arena string's bytes uninitialised

trigger: grapheme_strrpos() with a positive offset past the end of the haystack
notes: haystack is the argument zend_string's value array (zend_string_alloc(len,0), Zend/zend_string.h (master:190)); the empty-needle path did not range-check the offset before indexing it

trigger: NumberFormatter::format() on an array or an internal object with a cast_object handler
notes: the type was detected before convert_scalar_to_number_ex, so an IS_ARRAY zval (zend_array, Zend/zend_hash.c (master:289)) could be read through the INT32/DOUBLE branch

trigger: locale_get_primary_language()/locale_get_script() with a short or malformed locale string (bug #72241)
notes: loc_name is the argument zend_string's value array (zend_string_alloc(len,0), Zend/zend_string.h (master:190)); the grandfathered-tag scan indexed past its length

trigger: $dtdNamedNodeMap[$hugeIndex] on DTD entities or notations
notes: the index was taken as int and could overflow before being used to walk the libxml2 xmlHashTable holding the entities; xmlHashTable and its payloads come from libxml2's xmlMalloc (php-src never calls xmlMemSetup) libxml2 keeps its own allocator here: php-src never calls xmlMemSetup, which appears only in the Windows export list ext/libxml/php_libxml2.def (master:441).

trigger: read innerHTML / SimpleXML asXML on a document whose encoding is unavailable, producing an empty serialisation
notes: the empty result is the permanent interned empty zend_string (zend_string_alloc(len, 1) -> pemalloc(...,1) = malloc); RETURN_NEW_STR treats it as a fresh arena string and releases it, which is why the crash lands in zend_alloc.c

trigger: foreach over a DOMNodeList/DOMNamedNodeMap taking an early error path
notes: iterator = emalloc(sizeof(php_dom_iterator)) at ext/dom/dom_iterators.c:281 and the fix adds the missing memset - the arena does not scrub a recycled bin slot, so the fields held whatever the previous occupant left

trigger: getElementsByTagName() with a name containing an embedded NUL byte
notes: the xmlChar duplicate made by libxml2 (xmlStrdup, xmlMalloc memory) stops at the NUL and is shorter than the PHP length the traversal then uses libxml2 keeps its own allocator here: php-src never calls xmlMemSetup, which appears only in the Windows export list ext/libxml/php_libxml2.def (master:441).

trigger: registerPHPFunctions() then an XPath query calling a static method as 'Class::method'
notes: zend_make_callable turns fci.function_name from a zend_string into a zend_array (Zend/zend_hash.c (master:289), emalloc); zval_ptr_dtor_str then released an array through the string path

trigger: setAttributeNode() with an attribute node that is already attached to another element
notes: the attribute was linked into a second parent without being unlinked from the first, so both trees freed the same xmlAttr; libxml2 nodes come from xmlMalloc libxml2 keeps its own allocator here: php-src never calls xmlMemSetup, which appears only in the Windows export list ext/libxml/php_libxml2.def (master:441).

trigger: read a property on a DOM object whose prop_handler lookup fails
notes: tmp_member is a converted zval whose string payload is emalloc'd (Zend/zend_alloc.h (master:150)); the failure path in ext/dom/php_dom.c:232-255 released it on more than one exit

trigger: a hostile MySQL server sends a greeting packet whose auth plugin name is not NUL-terminated inside the packet
notes: estrdup((char*)p) ran strlen past the end of pfc->cmd_buffer.buffer, which is mnd_pemalloc(len, pfc->persistent) at ext/mysqlnd/mysqlnd_protocol_frame_codec.c (master:403) (emalloc when non-persistent)

trigger: connect with a password longer than the command buffer during an auth-switch
notes: the response is written into pfc->cmd_buffer.buffer (mnd_pemalloc, ext/mysqlnd/mysqlnd_protocol_frame_codec.c (master:403)) without checking the payload against the buffer length

trigger: a result set containing BIT columns whose declared sizes exceed the row data
notes: bit_area = row_buffer->ptr + data_size points past the row chunk; the chunk is carved out of the mysqlnd memory pool arena, itself mnd_emalloc'd (ext/mysqlnd/mysqlnd_block_alloc.c:70,90,120), so the write lands in a neighbouring chunk of the same block

trigger: hit memory_limit while freeing a buffered result set, then reach RSHUTDOWN
notes: the result rows are zvals duplicated with emalloc through the mysqlnd result set (mnd_emalloc -> emalloc, ext/mysqlnd/mysqlnd_alloc.c (master:73)); the bailout left them half-freed and RSHUTDOWN freed them again

trigger: a mysqlnd connection with protocol compression enabled
notes: compress_buf = mnd_emalloc(comp_buf_size) (ext/mysqlnd/mysqlnd_net.c at this revision (the file is mysqlnd_protocol_frame_codec.c on master)) was sent using the UNcompressed length, so uninitialised arena bytes beyond the compressed payload went out on the wire

trigger: a prepared statement whose bound parameters exceed mysqlnd.net_cmd_buffer_size (default 8k)
notes: the parameter block is written into pfc->cmd_buffer.buffer (mnd_pemalloc, ext/mysqlnd/mysqlnd_net.c at this revision, mysqlnd_protocol_frame_codec.c:403 on master; mnd_emalloc -> emalloc at ext/mysqlnd/mysqlnd_alloc.c (master:73)) without a size check, overwriting neighbouring bytes with 0x0; raising mysqlnd.net_cmd_buffer_size was the documented workaround

trigger: a hostile MySQL server sends a short or malformed error packet
notes: the fixed-size sqlstate array is a field of MYSQLND_ERROR_INFO embedded in the connection struct, which mysqlnd allocates with mnd_pecalloc (emalloc for a non-persistent connection, ext/mysqlnd/mysqlnd_alloc.c (master:73)); the copy was made without validating the packet length

trigger: a prepared statement fetched through a cursor
notes: the doubly-freed memory is the zval string payload copied out of the result set with mnd_emalloc -> emalloc (ext/mysqlnd/mysqlnd_alloc.c (master:73)); the PS path already owns the copy, so the extra copy_ctor/dtor pair released it twice

trigger: openssl_encrypt($data, 'aes-128-wrap-pad', ...) - AES key wrap with padding
notes: *poutbuf = zend_string_alloc((int)data_len + EVP_CIPHER_block_size(cipher_type), 0) at ext/openssl/openssl.c:7948 - the size ignores the RFC 5649 key-wrap-with-pad expansion, so EVP_CipherUpdate writes past the arena block. CVE-2026-14355; the advisory's own title is 'Memory corruption (zend_mm_heap corrupted)', naming the Zend allocator
