notes: ext/standard/image.c:424 buffer=emalloc(length) in php_read_APP (arena, input-sized by the marker's declared length); pre-fix php_read_stream_all_chunks() never advanced its local `buffer` pointer by read_now, so every chunk after the first overwrote the same leading bytes, leaving the tail of the emalloc'd buffer holding stale/uninitialized heap content that was then returned as if it were freshly read file data

trigger: call iptcembed() on a file (typically a pipe) that grows between the initial fstat() size check and the read/spool loop
notes: ext/standard/iptc.c:206 spoolbuf=zend_string_safe_alloc(1, iptcdata_len+sizeof(psheader)+1024+1, sb.st_size, 0) sizes the arena buffer from an fstat() taken before the read loop; pre-fix php_iptc_put1()/get1() did `*(*spoolbuf)++ = c;` with no check against the end of that allocation, so a file that grew past its stat'd size after the TOCTOU window overflowed spoolbuf's arena allocation

trigger: stream_poll() in grouped (non-raw) mode on a kqueue backend where merged read+write events for one fd need up to 2 kevent entries
notes: main/poll/poll_backend_kqueue.c:311 php_poll_realloc(backend_data->events, required_capacity*sizeof(struct kevent), ctx->persistent) expands via erealloc when ctx->persistent is false (main/poll/php_poll_internal.h:24-25, arena for the common non-persistent stream_poll() case, malloc otherwise); pre-fix the events buffer was only grown to 2x max_events for grouped mode while the kevent() call itself could still be asked to fill more slots than that in some paths, overflowing the arena buffer

trigger: verify an OpenSSL-signed phar whose signature/digest length is large enough that the (pre-fix) signed int output index overflows negative
notes: ext/phar/util.c:1334 *signature=(char*)safe_pemalloc(digest_len, 2, 1, PHAR_G(persist)) (pemalloc with persist=PHAR_G(persist), emalloc/arena in the common non-persistent-cache case); pre-fix `int pos=-1;` was used as the write index via `(*signature)[++pos]=...` for every hex nibble, so a large enough digest_len overflows pos negative, writing before the allocation

trigger: resolve a relative ("./...") phar path while PHAR_G(cwd_len) is larger than the path's own length
notes: ext/phar/phar.c:2077 (pre-fix) new_path=zend_string_alloc(path_length+path_length+1, false) sized the arena buffer from path_length twice instead of path_length+PHAR_G(cwd_len)+1; the next line, memcpy(ZSTR_VAL(new_path), PHAR_G(cwd), PHAR_G(cwd_len)), then writes PHAR_G(cwd_len) bytes into it, overflowing whenever the cwd is longer than the relative path

trigger: a phar fails validation (MAPPHAR_FAIL) after mydata is allocated but before its manifest/mounted_dirs/virtual_dirs tables are ever zend_hash_init'd
notes: ext/phar/phar.c:1091 mydata=pecalloc(1, sizeof(phar_archive_data), PHAR_G(persist)) (ecalloc/arena in the common non-persistent case) zero-fills the struct, but zend's HashTable uses a non-zero bit pattern (HT_INVALIDATE) to mean "never initialized" - a MAPPHAR_FAIL cleanup path that runs zend_hash_destroy() on the merely-zeroed manifest/mounted_dirs/virtual_dirs tables before they're ever real zend_hash_init'd treats that zeroed memory as a live, initialized HashTable

trigger: imageloadfont() on a stream (e.g. a user stream wrapper) that returns a short read while filling the font header
notes: ext/gd/gd.c:557 font=(gdFontPtr)emalloc(sizeof(gdFont)); pre-fix line 559 php_stream_read(stream, (char*)&font[b], hdr_size-b) indexed the gdFont* by b (scaling by sizeof(gdFont) via pointer arithmetic) instead of by the byte offset, so any short read that left b>0 made the next call's destination pointer land hdr_size-b bytes past the single-struct emalloc allocation

trigger: imageloadfont() on a font file whose byte-swapped w/h/nchars header fields multiply (overflow) to coincidentally match the already-mismatched body_size_check
notes: ext/gd/gd.c:1498 font->data=emalloc(body_size); body_size=font->w*font->h*font->nchars is recomputed after byte-swapping the header with no overflow guard, so a crafted header could make the swapped multiplication overflow to a small body_size that still equals body_size_check, after which the read loop below fills nchars*w*h real bytes into the undersized emalloc'd buffer

trigger: call imagecolormatch() on an image whose pixel indices (as produced by some image-reading paths) can reach or exceed im2->colorsTotal
notes: ext/gd/libgd/gd_color.c:36 (pre-fix) buf=(unsigned long*)safe_emalloc(sizeof(unsigned long),5*im2->colorsTotal,0); bp=buf+(color*5) is then indexed by color=im2->pixels[y][x], which some image-reading paths can set >= colorsTotal, writing past the arena buffer - fixed by a contributor

trigger: parse a HEIF/HEIC file whose "iinf" item box.size, added to box_offset, overflows past the end of the metadata buffer without the loop noticing
notes: ext/exif/exif.c:4410 data=(unsigned char*)emalloc(limit) in exif_scan_HEIF_header (arena, sized from the file's declared meta-box length); exif_isobmff_parse_meta() walks that buffer via `for (box_offset=data+4; box_offset<end-16; box_offset+=box.size)` - pre-fix there was no check that box_offset+box.size stays within [data,end) between iterations, so a large box.size advances box_offset past end before the loop condition catches it

trigger: parse a HEIF file whose parsed pos.offset+pos.size (from exif_isobmff_parse_meta's Exif item location) overflows the addition used to bound-check against FileSize
notes: ext/exif/exif.c data=(unsigned char*)emalloc(limit) (same arena buffer as php-0554); pre-fix the gate `(ImageInfo->FileSize >= pos.offset+pos.size)` could overflow so an invalid, oversized pos.size/pos.offset pair still passed, letting the code proceed to reseek/reread and compute `limit=pos.size-2` for a further stream read into `data`

trigger: an EXIF/TIFF tag whose component count is 0 (a legal-but-empty value) is read as if it held the tag's implied data width
notes: ext/exif/exif.c:2020 data=safe_emalloc(size,1,0) in exif_file_sections_add allocates the raw EXIF/APP1 segment (ImageInfo->file.list[n].data, arena); exif.c:3363 value_ptr=dir_entry+8 (dir_entry points into that same buffer) is used for byte_count<=4 tags including byte_count==0, and pre-fix several tag handlers (e.g. TAG_FNUMBER) called exif_convert_any_format()/exif_convert_any_to_int() on value_ptr without checking byte_count!=0 first, reading format-sized data (e.g. 8 bytes for a RATIONAL) from an inline slot that only guarantees 4 valid bytes

trigger: parse a TIFF/JPEG EXIF UserComment tag whose byte count leaves fewer than 2 bytes after the 8-byte 'UNICODE\0' prefix
notes: ext/exif/exif.c:1606 (data = safe_emalloc(size, 1, 0) in exif_file_sections_add) allocates the file-section buffer that offset_base/value_ptr point into; exif_process_user_comment memcmp'd 2 bytes past the ByteCount remaining without a length check first.

trigger: convert a string containing JISX0208 Kanji or JISX0201 Latin codepoints to CP50222
notes: ext/mbstring/libmbfl/mbfl/mbfl_encoding.h:146 (buf->str = emalloc(_ZSTR_STRUCT_SIZE(initsize)) in mb_convert_buf_init) backs buf->out/limit; MB_CONVERT_BUF_ENSURE reserved len+5 (Kanji, needs up to 6) / len+4 (Latin, needs up to 5) bytes, one short of the escape+shift+data sequence actually written.

trigger: convert a string with an ASCII/GB2312 state transition to HZ
notes: ext/mbstring/libmbfl/mbfl/mbfl_encoding.h:146 (buf->str = emalloc(...) in mb_convert_buf_init) backs the output buffer; the ASCII-shift path reserved len+2 but could write 3 bytes ('~','}',data byte) and the GB2312-shift path reserved len+2 but could write up to 4 bytes.

trigger: convert a codepoint needing a surrogate pair or a new BMP Base64 run to UTF-7 at the end of input
notes: ext/mbstring/libmbfl/mbfl/mbfl_encoding.h:146 (buf->str = emalloc(...) in mb_convert_buf_init) backs the output buffer; MB_CONVERT_BUF_ENSURE was raised from 6->7 bytes (surrogate pair path) and 3->4 bytes (BMP path) to cover the trailing pad byte. Same commit also fixes a STACK buffer overflow in mb_utf7_to_wchar writing past the 128-uint32_t wchar_buf local in mb_fast_convert (ext/mbstring/libmbfl/mbfl/mbfl_convert.c:352) -- out of scope, noted for completeness only.

trigger: a SOAP fault path (SoapFault, HTTP/connection error, SoapServer fault) runs on a ZTS worker thread other than the one that executed MINIT
notes: TSRM/TSRM.c:277 (p->storage[j] = malloc(...)) allocates each thread's module-globals block; the registered ctor php_soap_init_globals (ext/soap/soap.c) never set lang_en, which was instead assigned only once in PHP_MINIT_FUNCTION(soap); every ZTS worker thread but the one that ran MINIT read/dereferenced (and MSHUTDOWN even zend_string_release_ex'd) an uninitialized zend_string* field. Fix moves it to a plain non-globals static soap_lang_en.

trigger: pass a SoapHeader array to __soapCall containing a non-object element (e.g. an int)
notes: Zend/zend_objects_API.c:32 (objects->object_buckets = emalloc(init_size * sizeof(zend_object_store_bucket))) allocates EG(objects_store).object_buckets; Z_OBJPROP_PP(header) was called without first checking Z_TYPE_PP(header) == IS_OBJECT, so a non-object zval's raw union value was read as an object handle indexing object_buckets out of bounds.

trigger: scan a file whose libmagic pattern match contains many NUL or '~' bytes
notes: ext/fileinfo/libmagic/softmagic.c:1913 (t = zend_string_alloc(len * 2 + 4, 0)) undersized the escaped-pattern buffer: each NUL expands to 4 output chars but the formula only budgeted 2x+4, so the escaping loop wrote past the end of the zend_string.

trigger: load the magic database with the Zend Memory Manager disabled (USE_ZEND_ALLOC=0) and hit an OOM on the initial struct allocation
notes: ext/fileinfo/libmagic/apprentice.c:2604 (map = ecalloc(1, sizeof(*map))) -- on allocation failure (map stays NULL, only reachable in practice with ZMM disabled) the old code called efree(map) directly and then 'goto error', where apprentice_unmap(map) performs a second release/free pass over the same (NULL) map; fixed by a contributor

trigger: a magic-file FILE_PSTRING rule matches a pascal-style string near the end of a scanned buffer
notes: ext/fileinfo/libmagic/apprentice.c:463 (ms = ecalloc(1, sizeof(struct magic_set))) backs ms->ms_value (union VALUETYPE, file.h:404), whose s[MAXstring=64] array is p->s/ptr1; the pre-fix bound check 'len >= sizeof(p->s)' did not subtract the sz bytes already consumed by the pascal length prefix, letting the shift-left copy loop write past the 64-byte buffer.

trigger: scan a crafted ELF file whose note-header table runs past the buffered content
notes: ext/fileinfo/libmagic/magic.c:367 (buf = emalloc(HOWMANY + SLOP) in file_or_stream) backs the file-content buffer passed through file_buffer/file_tryelf as nbuf; donote() in readelf.c memcpy'd xnh_sizeof bytes from nbuf[offset] without first checking offset+xnh_sizeof against size (CVE-2014-3710).

trigger: regenerate/reset the session id a second time in the same request so the 'SID' constant already exists
notes: ext/session/session.c:1485/1493 (REGISTER_STRINGL_CONSTANT("SID", ..., 0) -> zend_register_stringl_constant -> zend_string_init, non-persistent, arena) creates the SID constant's value; php_session_reset_id() called zval_ptr_dtor_str(sid) (an unconditional Z_STR_P release) on the existing SID zval without checking Z_TYPE_P(sid) == IS_STRING first, fixed by switching to the type-dispatching zval_ptr_dtor().

trigger: an Apache MPM-worker thread other than the one that ran MINIT handles a session request
notes: TSRM/TSRM.c:277 (malloc) allocates each thread's session-module globals block; PHP_GINIT_FUNCTION(ps) (ext/session/session.c), the ctor run for every new thread, never set session_started_filename/session_started_lineno -- only PHP_MINIT_FUNCTION(session) did, once -- so any worker thread besides MINIT's read the uninitialized pointer field.

trigger: a ZTS worker thread other than the one that ran MINIT calls session_set_save_handler() logic that reads PS(set_handler)
notes: TSRM/TSRM.c:277 (malloc) allocates each thread's session-module globals block; PHP_GINIT_FUNCTION(ps) (ext/session/session.c) never zeroed set_handler, leaving it as uninitialized malloc'd bytes on every thread but the one that happened to set it explicitly.

trigger: submit a multipart upload whose field name is longer than the configured session.upload_progress.name ini value
notes: ext/session/session.c:880 (PHP_INI_ENTRY(...,"PHP_SESSION_UPLOAD_PROGRESS", ZEND_INI_PERDIR, OnUpdateString, rfc1867_name, ...) registers a persistent ini-entry string per the ini-entries precedent in ARENA-TEST.md); php_session_rfc1867_callback() memcmp'd name_len+1 bytes of PS(rfc1867_name) without first checking name_len == strlen(PS(rfc1867_name)), reading past the ini string when the uploaded field name was longer.

trigger: open a driver-specific persistent connection (e.g. new Pdo\Mysql(..., [PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT=>true])) via the static ::connect() path where a separate new_zval_object is constructed
notes: ext/pdo/pdo_dbh.c:1534 (dbh->inner = ecalloc(1, sizeof(pdo_dbh_t)) in pdo_dbh_new) allocates the pdo_dbh_t that dbh/Z_PDO_DBH_P(new_zval_object) points to; when switching to a cached/new persistent connection the old code did efree(dbh) and then repointed only php_pdo_dbh_fetch_object(current_object)->inner to the persistent pdbh, leaving new_zval_object->inner (the driver-specific object actually returned to userland) dangling at the just-freed dbh whenever current_object != new_zval_object.

trigger: an observer (e.g. Zend\Observer) inspects a PDO/PDOStatement internal method's run-time cache after connecting
notes: ext/pdo/pdo_dbh.c:1256 (ZEND_MAP_PTR(func.run_time_cache) = pemalloc(rt_cache_size, dbh->is_persistent), non-zeroing) backed each internal method's run-time cache slot -- emalloc/arena for an ordinary connection, malloc/system-malloc for PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT -- and was left uninitialized until _zend_observe_fcall_begin() read it; fixed by switching to the zeroing pecalloc().

trigger: open a new (not-yet-cached) persistent PDO connection
notes: EG(persistent_list) is a persistent HashTable (pemalloc(...,1)/malloc family per the 'persistent lists' row of ARENA-TEST.md); PDO::dbh_constructor (ext/pdo/pdo_dbh.c) built a stack-local zend_rsrc_list_entry le and copied it via zend_hash_str_update_mem(&EG(persistent_list), ..., &le, sizeof(le)) into that persistent table without first setting le's embedded refcount (GC_REFCOUNT(&le)), leaving the persistent list's own stored copy of the entry with uninitialized stack bytes as its refcount.

trigger: a query fails after PDOStatement construction but before/around statement execution (e.g. pdo_pgsql error retrieval on a failed query)
notes: ext/pdo/pdo_stmt.c:2187 (stmt = emalloc(sizeof(*stmt)) in pdo_dbstmt_new) allocates the pdo_stmt_t backing the PDOStatement object already stored in return_value by pdo_stmt_instantiate(); PDO::query()'s failure path called zval_dtor(return_value) (destroying/freeing that stmt object) while the pgsql driver's own error-retrieval logic still touched it during teardown, corrupting memory (bug #38535); fix removes the premature zval_dtor call and lets RETURN_FALSE overwrite return_value directly.

trigger: call ReflectionProperty::isReadable() on a dynamic/undeclared property name of a lazy or plain object (OSS-Fuzz #489355368)
notes: Zend/zend_hash.c:2488/2522 (zend_hash_real_init bucket array, pemalloc(...,0) -> arena) backs obj->properties, an ordinary object property HashTable whose bucket zvals can hold IS_UNDEF/typed values, not IS_PTR entries; ReflectionProperty::isReadable() (ext/reflection/php_reflection.c) called zend_hash_find_ptr(obj->properties, ...), a raw-pointer-hashtable accessor, and blindly read Z_PTR_P off whatever zval type was actually stored there. Fixed by switching to the type-safe zend_hash_find().

trigger: call ReflectionClass::getStaticPropertyValue() on a declared but not-yet-initialized typed static property
notes: Zend/zend_object_handlers.c:2115 (ZEND_MAP_PTR_SET(..., emalloc(sizeof(zval) * default_static_members_count)) in zend_class_init_statics) backs CE_STATIC_MEMBERS(ce); an uninitialized typed static property is stored there as an IS_UNDEF placeholder zval. zend_std_get_static_property(ce, name, BP_VAR_IS) does not throw on IS_UNDEF (unlike BP_VAR_R), and the reflection method did RETURN_COPY_DEREF(prop) unconditionally, copying the UNDEF zval's meaningless payload bytes out to userland.

trigger: instantiate an attribute whose argument list mixes positional and named arguments, and one argument's zend_get_attribute_value() fails after a named argument was already seen
notes: ext/reflection/php_reflection.c:6433 (args = emalloc(attr->data->argc * sizeof(zval))) allocates the positional-args buffer; on failure the cleanup call passed the loop index i (which also counts named args, stored separately in named_params) instead of argc (the count of args[] slots actually populated), so attribute_ctor_cleanup's zval_ptr_dtor loop read and released uninitialized emalloc'd zval slots.

trigger: index into (create a safe-array proxy for) a COM object's SAFEARRAY property
notes: ext/com_dotnet/com_handlers.c:647 (obj = emalloc(sizeof(*obj)) in php_com_object_new) allocates the php_com_dotnet_object whose embedded zo (zend_object) is the refcount target; php_com_saproxy_create() called Z_ADDREF_P(&proxy->obj->zo), a zval-refcount macro expecting a zval*, on a zend_object* instead -- it misread the object's inline refcount header as a zval value-union pointer and dereferenced that (effectively the small refcount integer) as an address, an arbitrary wild write. Fixed with the object-level GC_ADDREF().

trigger: destroy a COM/DOTNET/VARIANT wrapper object whose typeinfo field was never explicitly populated
notes: ext/com_dotnet/com_handlers.c:648 (obj = emalloc(sizeof(*obj))) allocates the php_com_dotnet_object; php_com_object_new() left obj->typeinfo unset on this path, and the object destructor does 'if (obj->typeinfo) ITypeInfo_Release(obj->typeinfo);' -- an uninitialized typeinfo is read as a live COM interface pointer and its vtable Release() slot is called through, a wild function-pointer dereference. Fixed by a contributor>typeinfo.

trigger: repeatedly invoke the same COM overloaded method by name so the method_cache lookup path is used
notes: ext/com_dotnet/com_handlers.c (ALLOC_HASHTABLE(obj->method_cache) -> emalloc(sizeof(HashTable)), Zend/zend_alloc.h:178) backs obj->method_cache; com_method_get() copies a stack-built zend_internal_function f (fn_flags left 0) via zend_hash_update(obj->method_cache, name, len, &f, sizeof(f), ...) into that heap cache and hands callers a further emalloc'd duplicate of it; without ZEND_ACC_CALL_VIA_HANDLER the engine's generic internal-call path mishandled the cached COM overloaded-dispatch function on reuse, corrupting memory (bug #60167).

trigger: load/cache a new COM type library by search string
notes: ext/com_dotnet/com_extension.c:218 (zend_ts_hash_init(&php_com_typelibraries, ..., persistent=1)) makes php_com_typelibraries a persistent malloc-family hashtable; php_com_load_typelib_via_cache() called zend_ts_hash_update(&php_com_typelibraries, ..., (void*)TL, sizeof(ITypeLib*), NULL), which copies sizeof(ITypeLib*) bytes starting at the address TL points to (out of the live COM object's own memory) instead of copying the pointer value TL itself; fixed by a contributor (void*)&TL. A later cache lookup then returned a garbage 'pointer' built from the COM object's leading bytes, causing heap corruption on next use (bug #39606).

trigger: set a phpdbg watchpoint (growing the internal address->watch b-tree through repeated insert_or_update calls)
notes: sapi/phpdbg/phpdbg_btree.c:159 (pemalloc((i+2)*sizeof(phpdbg_btree_branch), tree->persistent); phpdbg_btree_init sets tree->persistent=0 -> arena) allocates a chain of btree branch nodes; the pointer-chasing insert loop reassigned *branch each iteration while also advancing branch through it, leaving *branch one node short of the true leaf, so the trailing (*branch)->result.idx/ptr write landed on the wrong, already-linked node instead of the freshly emalloc'd leaf -- an out-of-bounds/misdirected write. Rewritten to walk a separate 'node' pointer and only write result fields on the confirmed last node. Same commit also fixes an OOB READ in phpdbg_check_watch_diff/WATCH_ON_BUCKET: packed-array elements are bare zvals, not Bucket structs, so reading Bucket.h/.key over-read the neighbouring HashTable slot (Zend/zend_hash.c bucket array, also arena).

trigger: set up phpdbg watchpoints a second time in the same process (e.g. after a prior watch cycle already flipped watchpoint_hit)
notes: PHPDBG_G(...) module-globals block (TSRM/TSRM.c:277 malloc, per the module-globals precedent) backs watchpoint_hit; phpdbg_setup_watchpoints() never reset it at (re-)setup, only relying on its process-start value, so a stale true from a prior watch cycle carried over.

trigger: run phpdbg's 'info classes' command while a user class with a parent is declared but not yet linked (parent class not encountered yet when the child was declared)
notes: Zend/zend.h:150-153 declares ce->parent as a union of zend_class_entry*/zend_string*, selected by ZEND_ACC_LINKED (parent_name, a zend_string see Zend/zend_string.h:190 zend_string_init -> arena, until linking; parent, a zend_class_entry*, after linking); PHPDBG_INFO(classes) (sapi/phpdbg/phpdbg_info.c) dereferenced ce->parent as a zend_class_entry* without checking ZEND_ACC_LINKED first, walking/reading class_entry-shaped fields (eventually reaching a zend_hash_num_elements() call) out of a much smaller zend_string allocation -- a heap buffer overflow.

trigger: print a formatted message whose vasprintf() result is an empty string (e.g. a format string starting with a NUL byte), reached via phpdbg's --run option
notes: sapi/phpdbg/phpdbg_out.c (msg = vasprintf(&msg, strfmt, args), a plain libc allocation freed via free(msg) right after) is malloc-family; when msglen==0, phpdbg_process_print(fd,type,msg,msglen) checked msg[msglen-1]=='\n', i.e. msg[-1], one byte before the malloc'd buffer. Fixed by a contributor==0.

trigger: run phpdbg's 'run' command with an inline argument list (e.g. 'run arg1 arg2')
notes: sapi/phpdbg/phpdbg_prompt.c: char *buf = emalloc(end - p + 1) undersized the per-argument copy buffer by one byte, because 'end' here points at the LAST character of the argument rather than one past it, so the copy loop plus its terminating NUL wrote one byte past the emalloc'd buffer; fixed by a contributor + 2 bytes.

trigger: access PHPDBG_G(cur_command) before any phpdbg command has explicitly set it
notes: TSRM/TSRM.c:279 (malloc) per-thread module-globals block backs PHPDBG_G(...); php_phpdbg_globals_ctor() (sapi/phpdbg/phpdbg.c), the ctor run for every new globals instance, never set cur_command, leaving it as uninitialized malloc'd bytes read as a stale/garbage pointer.

trigger: json_decode() a very long malformed string with JSON_INVALID_UTF8_SUBSTITUTE set, containing enough invalid UTF-8 bytes to overflow the per-scan invalid-byte counter
notes: ext/json/json_scanner.re:262 (size_t len = ... + s->utf8_invalid_count; str = zend_string_alloc(len, 0)) sizes the decoded JSON string buffer; s->utf8_invalid_count (an int, php_json_scanner.h:41) accumulated +2 per invalid UTF-8 byte substituted and could overflow on a very long malformed string, wrapping the computed len smaller than the bytes the substitution pass then writes into the zend_string_alloc'd buffer -- a heap buffer overflow write. Fixed by a contributor

trigger: call json_decode() with a $depth argument exceeding INT_MAX
notes: ext/json/JSON_parser.c: new_JSON_parser(int depth) allocates jp->stack = ecalloc(depth, sizeof(int)) and, for depth > JSON_PARSER_DEFAULT_DEPTH, jp->the_zstack = safe_emalloc(depth, sizeof(zval), 0); php_json_decode_ex() passed the full zend_long $depth through to this int parameter, silently truncating any value above INT_MAX to a mismatched (often much smaller or negative-then-huge) depth used to size these allocations versus the depth checks applied during parsing, an out-of-bounds write. Fixed by a contributor > INT_MAX up front.

trigger: a child process's stdout/stderr I/O event fires around the same time the child terminates and its record is freed
notes: sapi/fpm/fpm/fpm_children.c:45 (ret = malloc(sizeof(struct fpm_child_s))) allocates each child record; fpm_event_set() registered fpm_stdio_child_said with the raw child pointer as its event argument, so if the child was reaped/freed between scheduling and the event firing, the callback dereferenced a dangling struct fpm_child_s*. Fixed by a contributor>pid instead and re-resolving it via fpm_child_find(), returning early if the child is already gone.

trigger: FPM's zlog stream buffer needs to grow while appending a C string (an unused code path at the time of the fix, per the commit body)
notes: sapi/fpm/fpm/zlog.c:285 (zlog_stream_buf_alloc_ex: malloc(size)/realloc(stream->buf.data, size)) backs stream->buf.data; zlog_stream_buf_copy_cstr() requested growth to hold only str_len bytes instead of str_len + stream->len (the already-buffered content plus the new string), so the following memcpy(stream->buf.data + stream->len, str, str_len) could write past the reallocated buffer.

trigger: a worker child process exits/restarts under load, racing scoreboard slot allocation/free in the privileged root process
notes: sapi/fpm/fpm/fpm_scoreboard.c:58 (shm_mem = fpm_shm_alloc(scoreboard_size + scoreboard_nprocs_size)) backs the scoreboard's variable-sized procs array in FPM's own cross-process shared memory (mmap-based, outside the Zend heap -- no dedicated alloc_arena value exists for it, system-malloc is the closest 'non-Zend allocator' bucket); child->scoreboard_i was looked up indirectly through wp->scoreboard rather than resolved from the child record itself, letting a stale/mismatched (wp, index) pair read or write outside the live procs array from the privileged root process (bug #81026, CVE-class priv-esc). Fixed by a contributor

trigger: the web server/FastCGI client closes the connection mid-response so a write()/send() on the fcgi fd fails and fcgi_write() returns a negative ssize_t
notes: sapi/fpm/fpm/fpm_main.c:299-308 (sapi_cgibin_ub_write(): ptr += ret; remaining -= ret;) walks through PHP's own output data (typically a zend_string from output buffering, arena, input-sized); fcgi_write()'s error return (a negative ssize_t, e.g. -1) was captured into sapi_cgibin_single_write's `size_t ret`, sign-converting it to a huge unsigned value, so ptr advanced far past the end of the actual output buffer and the unsigned `remaining` counter underflowed, causing the next write() to read and transmit out-of-bounds process memory to the client (bug #60629).

trigger: a ZTS CGI/FastCGI build hits a hard startup error (e.g. a missing extension .dll/.so) during the extension-registration phase, before MINIT(cgi) has run
notes: TSRM/TSRM.c:277 (malloc) allocates each thread's module-globals block once ts_allocate_id() has registered it; ts_allocate_id(&php_cgi_globals_id, ...) was only called from PHP_MINIT_FUNCTION(cgi), so any CGIG(...) access (e.g. from the logging path) before MINIT ran read from a not-yet-registered/uninitialized TSRM slot. Fixed by moving the ts_allocate_id() call to main(), before sapi_startup().

trigger: run a php-cgi script whose first line starts with '#' but has no LF/CR before the end of the mmap'd file
notes: sapi/cgi/cgi_main.c: for ZEND_HANDLE_MAPPED file handles, file_handle.handle.stream.mmap.buf is an OS mmap() of the script file, not the Zend heap (no dedicated alloc_arena value exists for a raw mmap, system-malloc is the closest non-Zend bucket); the shebang-skipping loop 'while (c != NEWLINE && c != CR && c != EOF) c = buf[i++];' had no bound tied to mmap.len, so a file with no trailing newline let i run past the mapped region (bug #68618).

trigger: call apache_request_headers() while an HTTP_* environment variable name contains '=' or specific trailing-underscore patterns
notes: sapi/cgi/cgi_main.c:1612 (t = emalloc(alloc_size)/erealloc(t, alloc_size), alloc_size = var_len + 64) backs the per-header name-transform buffer t/q; the underscore-to-dash and case-folding loop had no explicit end-of-name check besides the NUL terminator, so a name containing '=' or trailing underscores could read past the source and write past q's allocated capacity. Fixed by a contributor '=' and guarding the post-underscore uppercase copy (bug #61807).

trigger: serve a CGI/FastCGI request under a per-dir/user-ini configuration whose translated script path needs a trailing slash appended after zend_dirname() truncation
notes: sapi/cgi/cgi_main.c:726 (path = estrndup(SG(request_info).path_translated, path_len), allocating path_len+1 bytes) backed path; when a trailing slash needed appending, 'path[path_len++] = DEFAULT_SLASH; ... path[path_len] = 0;' wrote the NUL terminator at index path_len+1, one byte past the estrndup'd allocation -- a heap off-by-one overflow. Fixed by a contributor+2 bytes (emalloc) whenever a slash needs appending.

trigger: call hash_pbkdf2() with an output $length argument large enough (past 2^24) that the float-based ceil() computations of digest_length/loops lose precision
notes: ext/hash/hash.c:1051 (result = safe_emalloc(loops, ops->digest_size, 0)) sizes the PBKDF2 digest buffer; digest_length and loops were computed via ceil((float) length / 2.0) and ceil((float) digest_length / digest_size) -- a float's 24-bit mantissa rounds incorrectly once length exceeds 2^24, so loops*digest_size could come out smaller than the digest actually produced, and zend_bin2hex() (hex-encoding result into the return string) then wrote past the end of that under-sized emalloc'd buffer; rounding the other way instead left the tail of the returned string uninitialized. Fixed with exact integer arithmetic (length/2 + length%2, and (digest_length-1)/digest_size + 1).

trigger: unserialize() a crafted HashContext for the xxh32 algorithm whose internal memsize field is between 16 and 31
notes: ext/hash/php_hash.h:158 (return ecalloc(1, ops->context_size) in php_hash_alloc_context) allocates hash->context, e.g. a PHP_XXH32_CTX; php_hash_xxh32_unserialize() (introduced by the sibling fix, php-0654, for oss-fuzz #29538) validated ctx->s.memsize < 32, but xxh32's internal buffer (ctx->s.mem) is only 16 bytes -- a copy-paste of the xxh64 (32-byte) bound -- so a crafted serialized context with 16 <= memsize < 32 passed validation and a later hash update/final could write past the 16-byte buffer.

trigger: unserialize() a crafted HashContext for xxh32/xxh64 with an out-of-range internal memsize field
notes: ext/hash/php_hash.h:158 (return ecalloc(1, ops->context_size)) allocates hash->context (a PHP_XXH32_CTX/PHP_XXH64_CTX); before this fix xxh32/xxh64 used the generic php_hash_unserialize with no bound on ctx->s.memsize at all, so a crafted serialized HashContext could set memsize past the internal mem[] buffer's real size, and a later update/final call would use memsize as a copy length -- an out-of-bounds write. Fixed by a contributor (oss-fuzz #29538); the xxh32 bound was itself wrong (32 instead of 16) until the follow-up fix, php-0653.

trigger: call mhash_keygen_s2k() with a huge $bytes argument (a long) on a 64-bit build
notes: ext/hash/hash.c:786 (key = ecalloc(1, times * block_size), times = (int)(bytes / block_size)) sizes the derived-key buffer; bytes was a 64-bit long used directly (untruncated) later in RETVAL_STRINGL(key, bytes, 1) and memset(key, 0, bytes), while 'int times' silently truncated that same bytes value when computing the actual ecalloc size -- a sufficiently large bytes made times wrap to a small/negative int, leaving the ecalloc'd key buffer far smaller than the bytes-sized memset/RETVAL_STRINGL that followed it, a heap buffer overflow read+write. Fixed by a contributor, up front, so every use is consistent.

trigger: call hash_final() on a hash resource whose context is later reused/finalized again (e.g. via the resource destructor's own internal hash_final call, or a second explicit hash_final() call)
notes: ext/hash/hash.c:165 (context = emalloc(ops->context_size); hash->context = context;) allocates the algorithm context; hash_final() (PHP_FUNCTION) previously left hash->context non-NULL and un-freed after producing the digest, so the resource destructor php_hash_dtor's own hash_final()+efree(hash->context) call (or a second explicit hash_final()) operated on/freed a context whose lifetime had already effectively ended -- a double free. Fixed by having hash_final() itself efree(hash->context) and set it NULL, and guarding the destructor's cleanup on hash->context being non-NULL.

trigger: parse an XML document whose accumulated CDATA/character-data content approaches size_t wraparound on a 32-bit build
notes: ext/xml/xml.c: Z_STR_P(myval) = zend_string_extend(Z_STR_P(myval), newlen, 0), where newlen = Z_STRLEN_P(myval) + ZSTR_LEN(decoded_value) was computed as a plain size_t addition that could wrap on 32-bit builds; the following strncpy(..., ZSTR_LEN(decoded_value)+1) then wrote the full new chunk length into the under-sized zend_string_extend'd (arena, zend_string_alloc family) buffer regardless -- a heap buffer overflow. Fixed by switching to the bounds-checked zend_string_safe_realloc().

trigger: parse an XML document via the xml compat (SAX) API with enough attributes on one element to overflow (nb_attributes*2)+1 (currently capped well below that by libxml, per the commit body)
notes: ext/xml/compat.c: attrs = safe_emalloc((nb_attributes * 2) + 1, sizeof(int *), 0) computed (nb_attributes*2)+1 as a plain, unchecked multiplication before handing the already-multiplied value to safe_emalloc, so safe_emalloc's own overflow check covered the wrong (already-wrapped) operand rather than the real multiplication. Fixed by a contributor 2*sizeof(int*) as separate safe_emalloc operands, with sizeof(int*) as its overflow-checked additive term.

trigger: pass a reference or a wrongly-typed array as the xml_parse_into_struct() output, then let a handler mutate it
notes: the parser's zvals (parser->data/info/index and the arrays they hold) are emalloc'd zend_arrays (Zend/zend_hash.c (master:289)); the referenced value was copied without a refcount and used without type checks

trigger: xml_parse_into_struct() hitting the memory_limit before the first level tag is stored
notes: parser->ltags = safe_emalloc(XML_MAXLEVEL, sizeof(char *), 0) at ext/xml/xml.c:1365 was never zeroed, and the arena does not scrub recycled slots, so xml_parser_free_ltags efree'd whatever pointers the previous occupant left

trigger: xml_parser_set_option($p, XML_OPTION_SKIP_TAGSTART, <huge>) then parse a document
notes: toffset is an int and the long option value overflows it; str + toffset then indexes past the tag-name string, which expat allocates through PHP's own handlers (php_xml_malloc_wrapper -> emalloc, ext/xml/xml.c (master:201)). GHSA-wg4p-4hqh-c3g9 later cited this commit

trigger: any Windows path API called with an empty path string
notes: path[path_len - 1] with path_len == 0 indexes (size_t)-1 before the zend_string value array the caller passed (zend_string_alloc(len,0), Zend/zend_string.h (master:190))

trigger: PHP startup on Windows with per-directory registry configuration
notes: data = (zval*)malloc(sizeof(zval)) at win32/registry.c:87 for the persistent registry cache; Z_TYPE was never set, so the ini machinery read a type byte from uninitialised malloc memory

trigger: Windows registry configuration with subkey names longer than the queried maximum
notes: name = emalloc(max_key + 1) and new_path = emalloc(path_len + max_key + 2) at win32/registry.c:123-124; RegEnumKeyEx was called with a length that did not match those buffers

trigger: new PDO('sqlite:x') with a DSN filename shorter than ':memory:'
notes: memcmp(filename, ":memory:", sizeof(":memory:")-1) reads 8 bytes from the DSN string, which came from the argument zend_string (zend_string_alloc(len,0), Zend/zend_string.h (master:190)), without first checking its length

trigger: any pdo_sqlite error, then the handle teardown
notes: einfo->errmsg was assigned the string returned by sqlite3_errmsg(H->db), which libsqlite3 owns, and the error-info teardown passes einfo->errmsg to efree - a libsqlite3 pointer handed to the Zend allocator. The fix copies it with pestrdup php-src never calls sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_MALLOC), so libsqlite3 uses its own allocator; the PHP wrapper beside it is arena (zend_object_alloc, Zend/zend_objects_API.h (master:93)).

trigger: ftp_get() in FTP_ASCII mode from a server that places '\r' at the last byte of a full FTP_BUFSIZE read
notes: the lookahead *(s+1) reads one byte past data->buf, which is char buf[FTP_BUFSIZE] inline in the emalloc'd databuf_t (ext/ftp/ftp.h:46), so it reads the next field or the neighbouring arena slot; reported by ASAN as heap-buffer-overflow read of size 1

trigger: ftp_rawlist()/ftp_nlist() against a server returning more list data than fits an int
notes: size and rcvd were ints and could overflow before ret = safe_emalloc((lines + 1), sizeof(char*), size) at ext/ftp/ftp.c:1682, so the copy ran past the undersized arena block (bug #69545)

trigger: dba_open() on a flatfile database with a malformed (e.g. negative) length prefix
notes: buf = erealloc(buf, buf_size) at ext/dba/libflatfile/flatfile.c:118,141 grows the buffer only to the atoi()-narrowed length, so the subsequent read runs past the arena block

trigger: any dba_open() on a 32-bit build
notes: zend_object_alloc(sizeof(dba_info), class_type) at ext/dba/dba.c:311 allocated the object using the size of the WRONG struct, so every write to the dba_connection fields past sizeof(dba_info) landed outside the bin slot; the fix uses sizeof(dba_connection)

trigger: a Random\Engine implementation whose generate() returns a reference
notes: retval was read as a zend_string without dereferencing the zend_reference (Zend/zend_string.h (master:190) for the string, the reference itself emalloc'd), so a zend_reference was used through the string layout

trigger: socket_read($sock, $len, PHP_NORMAL_READ) on a socket that returns no data
notes: the loop tests *t before anything is written into the destination, which socket_read allocates as zend_string_alloc(length, 0) (Zend/zend_string.h (master:190)); the arena does not zero recycled memory, so the loop terminated on stale bytes

trigger: php -S with PHP_CLI_SERVER_WORKERS set to a very large value
notes: php_cli_server_workers is a malloc'd array (free(php_cli_server_workers) at sapi/cli/php_cli_server.c:2301) whose element count came unvalidated from the environment variable

trigger: php -S binding to a host that resolves to several addresses where an early bind fails
notes: sa is freed with pefree(sa, 1), i.e. libc free (sapi/cli/php_cli_server.c:912); it was not NULLed, so the next loop iteration freed the same block again

trigger: wddx_deserialize() of a packet whose <char> element has no code attribute
notes: the atts array is built by the XML compat layer with attrs = safe_emalloc((nb_attributes * 2) + 1, sizeof(int *), 0) at ext/xml/compat.c:173; php_wddx_push_element indexed atts[i+1] without checking it was present (bug #73065)

trigger: wddx_deserialize() of a packet declaring a class name on a non-object element
notes: ent2->data is a zval whose payload is a zend_array/zend_object (Zend/zend_hash.c (master:289), Zend/zend_objects.c (master:190)); HASH_OF was taken before the type was validated (bug #71335)

trigger: a session whose serialize_handler is wddx, with a crafted session payload
notes: the deserialized entry zvals are emalloc'd and pushed on the wddx stack with wddx_stack_push (ext/wddx/wddx.c:69-75 macro region); the entry was used through the wrong type's accessors (bug #70741)

trigger: filter_var() with FILTER_SANITIZE_ENCODED on a string longer than ZEND_LONG_MAX/3
notes: str = zend_string_alloc(3 * Z_STRLEN_P(value), 0) at ext/filter/sanitizing_filters.c:90 overflows before the allocation, so the encoding loop writes past the arena block (bug #71637)

trigger: msg_send() with a very large serialized message
notes: messagebuffer = safe_emalloc(maxsize, 1, sizeof(struct php_msgbuf)) at ext/sysvmsg/sysvmsg.c:367 with the length held in the wrong (narrower) integer type, so the copy overran the arena block (bug #78819)

trigger: msg_receive() with unserialize enabled on a corrupted System V message
notes: tmp is a zval from MAKE_STD_ZVAL (emalloc, Zend/zend_alloc.h (master:150)); when php_var_unserialize fails at ext/sysvmsg/sysvmsg.c:341 it is left with an uninitialised type byte and was still returned/destroyed

trigger: iconv_mime_decode() on a header with a crafted encoded-word length
notes: the look-ahead offset arithmetic overflows and indexes past the input zend_string's value array (zend_string_alloc(len,0), Zend/zend_string.h (master:190)) (bug #78069)

trigger: mcrypt_generic() with a very large data string
notes: data_size = (((data_len - 1) / block_size) + 1) * block_size at ext/mcrypt/mcrypt.c:694 can overflow, and data_s = emalloc(data_size + 1) at :695/:700/:740 is then undersized for the cipher's write (bug #72455)

trigger: mcrypt_generic_init() with an IV of the wrong size
notes: key_s = emalloc(key_len) at ext/mcrypt/mcrypt.c:606; the wrong-IV error path returned without the buffers being consistently owned, leaving a freed arena buffer referenced and read past its end

trigger: mcrypt_encrypt()/mcrypt_decrypt() with a key longer than the cipher's key size
notes: key_s = emalloc(use_key_length) at ext/mcrypt/mcrypt.c:1194 then memcpy of a different length; the two could differ

trigger: PDO::lastInsertId() on a table whose IDENTITY column is numeric(p,0) with p above ~30
notes: id = emalloc(32) at ext/pdo_dblib/dblib_driver.c:270 and dbconvert() was called with a destination length of -1, which disables FreeTDS's own bounds check, so a longer textual value overran the 32-byte bin slot

trigger: PDOStatement::getColumnMeta($n) with a column number past the result's column count
notes: the column arrays are FreeTDS/dblib internals reached through dbcolname()/dbcoltype() on H->link and allocated by the client library's own allocator; colno was not range-checked, unlike the emalloc'd S->cols array beside it (ext/pdo_dblib/dblib_stmt.c) the PHP-side wrapper object beside it IS arena (zend_object_alloc, Zend/zend_objects_API.h (master:93)) - it is not the object this bug touched.

trigger: bcround($num, PHP_INT_MAX) or BcMath\Number::round() with an extreme precision
notes: the unchecked precision drives the length passed to _bc_new_num_nonzeroed_ex, which allocates with pemalloc(required_size, persistent) at ext/bcmath/libbcmath/src/init.c:50 (emalloc when non-persistent); the signed overflow then makes round.c write outside it

trigger: pcntl_exec() with an environment pair whose key plus value length overflows int
notes: pair_length was an int used to size the emalloc'd env pair buffer (ext/pcntl/pcntl.c:958 area); the fix switches to size_t and safe_emalloc (bug #79812)

trigger: sodium_crypto_generichash_init() then returning/serialising the state string
notes: state = zend_string_alloc(state_len, 0) at ext/sodium/libsodium.c:942 with state_len = sizeof(crypto_generichash_state) (:916), but libsodium initialises fewer bytes than that padded struct, so the trailing bytes memcpy'd out and handed to userland were whatever the arena slot last held (bug #78510)

trigger: ereg_replace() with a replacement containing many backreferences
notes: buf = safe_emalloc(buf_len, sizeof(char), 0) at ext/ereg/ereg.c:438 is sized before the backreference expansion, so the copy ran past it (bug #73284)

trigger: a regular expression whose compiled strip needs more space than the initial estimate
notes: g = (struct re_guts *)malloc(sizeof(struct re_guts) + (NC-1)*sizeof(cat_t)) at ext/ereg/regex/regcomp.c:116 and p->ssize was computed with a formula that could underestimate; the bundled regex library uses libc malloc, not emalloc (bug #69248)

trigger: unbuffered sybase_ct queries where a result is cleaned up twice
notes: the sybase_result structs are emalloc'd (the fix introduces efree_n/efree_if macros that NULL the pointer after efree, ext/sybase_ct/php_sybase_ct.c:139-140)

trigger: a persistent mysql_pconnect() link torn down at shutdown
notes: a persistent php_mysql_conn must outlive the request and is therefore malloc'd, not emalloc'd (Zend/zend_alloc.h (master:188) pemalloc with persistent=1); the close handler released it on a path where the persistent-list destructor also freed it

trigger: parse a file: URL with an empty or truncated host component (Uri\WhatWg\Url or DOM URL parsing)
notes: the over-read is inside lexbor's URL parser, and php-src repoints ALL of lexbor at the Zend allocator: lexbor_memory_setup(php_lexbor_malloc, ...) at ext/lexbor/php_lexbor.c (master:61) with php_lexbor_malloc returning emalloc(size) at ext/lexbor/php_lexbor.c:30-33

trigger: mhash_keygen_s2k($hash, $pass, $salt, $bytes) with a negative or huge $bytes
notes: ret = emalloc(bytes + 1) at ext/mhash/mhash.c:226 with an unvalidated user long; mhash_keygen_ext then writes bytes into it, so a negative or wrapping value undersizes the arena block

trigger: mail() with mail.mixed_lf_and_crlf / cr_lf_mode 'lf' and an empty message body
notes: the loop bound msg_len - 1 underflows to SIZE_MAX when the message is empty, so the scan runs off the message string before converted_message = emalloc(msg_len - new_len + 1) at ext/standard/mail.c:626 is even sized correctly

trigger: compile a source file containing a single string literal of 2 GB or more
notes: yyleng is unsigned int but len in zend_scan_escape_string was int, so a >=2GB literal wraps negative; the target zend_string for such a literal exceeds ZEND_MM_MAX_LARGE_SIZE and therefore comes from zend_mm_alloc_huge (Zend/zend_alloc.c:1924), its own chunk-aligned mmap - one of the few PHP objects that does get its own mapping

trigger: Windows: dirname() style path handling on a path whose first byte is a slash
notes: IS_SLASH_P(end) may read end[-1], one byte before the path buffer; the path is ZSTR_VAL of a caller zend_string (zend_string_alloc(len,0), Zend/zend_string.h (master:190)). The fix adds IS_SLASH_P_EX with a guard

trigger: a consumer (e.g. mailparse) calling php_stream_memory_get_buffer() and treating the result as a C string
notes: ms->data is a zend_string grown with zend_string_realloc at main/streams/memory.c:56; the write path never re-terminated it, so consumers read past ZSTR_LEN into the rest of the arena block

trigger: sscanf() with an XPG positional specifier whose argument number is INT_MIN or otherwise extreme
notes: objIndex = value - 1 was computed before the range check, so a negative index was used against nassign = safe_emalloc(sizeof(int), numVars, 0) at ext/standard/scanf.c:322

trigger: clone an InternalIterator instance
notes: create_object was overridden to zend_internal_iterator_create (Zend/zend_interfaces.c:665) but clone_obj was not, so the clone was allocated with the standard handler's size and freed with the internal one - a size/handler mismatch on an emalloc'd zend_object (Zend/zend_objects_API.h (master:93))

trigger: destroy a generator that is suspended inside a try block with a finally, so the dtor jumps to the finally
notes: the generator's frame and CV slots live in stack = emalloc(used_stack * sizeof(zval)) at Zend/zend_generators.c:73 (the zend_generator itself at :398); the finally path indexed a CV of a frame that had already been cleaned up

trigger: [...$a, ...$b] unpacking packed arrays into a packed result
notes: zend_hash_extend(result_ht, ...) at Zend/zend_vm_def.h:6131 was given the number of USED slots rather than the number of elements, so the packed bucket array (emalloc'd, Zend/zend_hash.c (master:224)) was too small for the writes that followed

trigger: ini_set('open_basedir', ...) at runtime with a value ending in a partial '..' component
notes: the scan loop was while(true) with no NUL check, running past ptr = pathbuf = estrdup(ZSTR_VAL(new_value)) at main/fopen_wrappers.c:97

trigger: fgetcsv() with a NUL byte as the delimiter or enclosure
notes: bptr = buf where buf = php_stream_get_line(stream, NULL, 0, &buf_len) at ext/standard/file.c:2036,2067 - an emalloc'd line buffer; the isspace() scan walked past limit because inc_len was 1 for the NUL case (oss-fuzz #57392)

trigger: crypt($pw, '$2') - a bcrypt salt cut short after two characters
notes: salt[3] was read after only salt[0] and salt[1] had been validated, running past the salt zend_string's value array (zend_string_alloc(len,0), Zend/zend_string.h (master:190))

trigger: preg_replace() producing a replacement close to SIZE_MAX
notes: alloc_len = zend_safe_address_guarded(2, new_len, 0) at ext/pcre/php_pcre.c:1728 did not account for the zend_string header, so the following zend_string_alloc could wrap and undersize the arena block (bug #74604)

trigger: str_repeat()/concatenation producing a length near SIZE_MAX
notes: result_str = zend_string_alloc(result_len, 0) at Zend/zend_operators.c:1899 with result_len only slightly below SIZE_MAX wraps once the zend_string header is added, so the copy runs past the block (bug #74960; ZSTR_MAX_LEN is introduced by this fix)

trigger: Windows: PharData::extractTo() on an entry whose filename contains backslashes
notes: the do/while ran while (cnt++ <= filename_len), one past the end of the entry filename buffer, and wrote '/' there; the filename is emalloc'd request memory carried on the phar_entry_info (ext/phar/phar_object.c:4155 region)

trigger: strip_tags() on input beginning with a quote inside a tag
notes: *(p-1) was read with p at the start of the buffer, one byte before rbuf, which strip_tags allocates as a zend_string copy of the input (zend_string_alloc(len,0), Zend/zend_string.h (master:190))

trigger: $str[PHP_INT_MIN] - a string offset at the extreme negative
notes: (size_t)((offset < 0) ? -offset : (offset + 1)) overflows for ZEND_LONG_MIN, so the bounds check passed and the read indexed outside the zend_string's value array (Zend/zend_string.h (master:190))

trigger: pack() with a repeat count that makes currentarg + arg overflow int
notes: currentarg + arg overflowed before being used to index the argument array, which zpp allocates as an emalloc'd zval array; the fix adds currentarg > INT_MAX - arg (bug #78833)

trigger: mb_eregi() with a pattern whose compiled exact-string node is shorter than the buffer assumed
notes: the compiled regex node buffer belongs to the bundled oniguruma, which uses libc malloc directly: #define xmalloc malloc at ext/mbstring/oniguruma/src/regint.h:99 (php-src does not repoint it, unlike mbfl which uses emalloc)

trigger: exif_read_data() on a JPEG whose embedded thumbnail is under 4 bytes
notes: ImageInfo->Thumbnail.data is estrndup'd at ext/exif/exif.c:2559 (or safe_emalloc at :3752); the scanner read the 2-byte marker and length without checking Thumbnail.size

trigger: opcache optimizer running SCCP over a function where a definition is removed
notes: the SSA arrays it indexes are allocated from the optimizer's zend_arena (zend_arena_calloc on ctx.arena, ext/opcache/Optimizer/zend_optimizer.c), which is emalloc'd via zend_arena_create (Zend/zend_arena.h (master:35))

trigger: compile a constant array literal containing a spread element, e.g. [1, ...$a]
notes: elem_ast->child[1] was read although an UNPACK element has only one child; zend_ast nodes are bump-allocated from CG(ast_arena) (zend_arena_alloc, Zend/zend_arena.h (master:66), itself emalloc'd at :35), so the read lands in a neighbouring AST node

trigger: exif_read_data() on a crafted thumbnail whose marker sits at the very end
notes: php_jpg_get16 read two bytes at pos without checking pos against ImageInfo->Thumbnail.size; the buffer is estrndup'd at ext/exif/exif.c:2559 (bug #77988)

trigger: exif_read_data() on a file whose IFD entry offset points before offset_base
notes: value_ptr = offset_base + offset_val was dereferenced (and _estrndup'd from) without checking that dir_entry > offset_base; the section data is emalloc'd request memory in ImageInfo->file.list[sn].data (bug #77950) The section buffer is allocated by exif_file_sections_add: data = safe_emalloc(size, 1, 0); at ext/exif/exif.c:1606.

trigger: exif_read_data() on a file with a tag whose declared length exceeds the section
notes: the value is copied out of the emalloc'd EXIF section buffer (ImageInfo->file.list[sn].data) using a length taken from the file (bug #77831) The section buffer is allocated by exif_file_sections_add: data = safe_emalloc(size, 1, 0); at ext/exif/exif.c:1606.

trigger: exif_read_data() on a file with a crafted maker note
notes: php_ifd_get32s read past the maker-note value buffer, which lives inside the emalloc'd EXIF section data; the size check did not cover every path (bug #77753) The section buffer is allocated by exif_file_sections_add: data = safe_emalloc(size, 1, 0); at ext/exif/exif.c:1606.

trigger: an error message long enough that the smart_string growth arithmetic wraps
